docs.title: Myconote_CLI
docs.text:
Blazing-fast fungal genome annotation pipeline -- as fungal genome sequencing becomes cheaper and long-read assemblies routine, the bottleneck has shifted from sequencing to annotation. Existing pipelines are slow, fragile, and leave outputs that take days of manual cleanup before NCBI will accept them. myconote-cli addresses this gap: a high-performance Rust CLI that takes a fungal genome assembly from raw contigs to an NCBI-ready submission, integrating 15 annotation sources with built-in validation and reproducibility tracking.

The tool runs on other eukaryotes, but defaults, benchmarks, and the learn tutorial are tuned for fungi.

Developed by Benjamin Narh-Madey - Hittinger Lab, Laboratory of Genetics - UW-Madison

docs.title: What is Myconote_CLI?
docs.text:
Myconote_CLI takes a genome assembly (FASTA) through a structured, reproducible annotation pipeline:

Sort -> Mask -> Train -> Predict -> Update -> Annotate -> Submit

Each step is a separate subcommand, giving you full control over where to start, pause, or resume. All intermediate files use standard formats (GFF3, FASTA, GenBank) compatible with Proksee (web), IGV (desktop), and clinker (cross-species gene-cluster synteny) — the tools MycoNote hands off to rather than reimplementing.

RNA-seq is a first-class input at four distinct points: train and update use reads as evidence for gene models; quant uses reads for expression quantification (salmon + decoy-aware index, tximport-ready outputs); fetch-rna pulls reads by SRA/ENA accession so the entire RNA-seq stack runs end-to-end from an accession list.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Fastest prediction, competitive accuracy -- in a four-tool benchmark (vs funannotate, MAKER, BRAKER; 6 fungal genomes × 3 reps), MycoNote has the fastest gene prediction (~3× funannotate) and is ~2× faster end-to-end at matched functional output; accuracy is competitive (BRAKER3 leads overall). See the benchmark.
  • 26 CLI commands covering the full fungal genome annotation lifecycle
  • 11 annotation sources -- MMseqs2 (Swiss-Prot), Pfam (hmmsearch), InterProScan, EggNOG, CAZyme (dbCAN), MEROPS, BUSCO, antiSMASH, tRNAscan-SE, secretome, GO terms
  • Multi-tool gene prediction -- Augustus, SNAP, GlimmerHMM, GeneMark, miniprot protein evidence, agreement-weighted consensus
  • RNA-seq expression quantification -- quant wraps fastp + salmon with a decoy-aware index, emits tximport-ready quant.sf per sample plus wide count and TPM matrices
  • DESeq2 differential expression -- de-template emits a ready-to-run R script (tximport → DESeq2 → apeglm shrinkage → volcano + MA plots); no R runtime dependency in the CLI itself
  • SRA / ENA ingestion -- fetch-rna pulls public RNA-seq by run, study, BioProject, sample, or experiment accession; ENA REST default, sra-toolkit fallback
  • AI-powered interpretation -- explain uses a local LLM (Ollama) to interpret results with grounded citations and command recommendations. No data leaves your machine.
  • Multi-genome batch mode -- batch annotates many genomes from a directory or sample sheet with HTCondor support, resume capability, and a live dashboard
  • 25 NCBI genetic code tables -- tables 1–6, 9–14, 16, 21–31, 33, every table verified against the NCBI reference. Critical for Candida CTG clade (Table 12) and other yeast-specific codes; includes caveats for context-dependent tables 27, 28, 31
  • NCBI submission prep -- GFF3 validation, .tbl generation, table2asn integration
  • Ploidy awareness -- allelic duplicate detection for polyploid genomes
  • N-genome orthology -- compare wraps OrthoFinder with tiered genome-count caps tuned for fungal clades (5 fungi / 3 small plants / 2 large)
  • 15+ format conversions -- GFF3/GTF/BED/GenBank/FASTA/FASTQ/PHYLIP/NEXUS/VCF, plus convert --to cds for spliced transcriptome extraction
  • Interactive tutorial -- myconote-cli learn (swirl-style, terminal-based)
  • Reproducibility -- workflow reports (JSON), per-run bundles for quant and explain, database version tracking, output validation
  • Docker + Singularity containers for HPC and cloud environments
  • CI/CD -- GitHub Actions (fmt, clippy, test, build, security audit)
  • 500+ tests passing on real fungal genome data (Brettanomyces bruxellensis, Candida tropicalis)

docs.title: Multi-kingdom note
docs.text: --kingdom plant|animal|insect|protist continues to work because the non-fungal Augustus species lists, BUSCO lineages, and intron-size ranges are still registered in the code. They are not validated on large non-fungal genomes and are not a supported use case at this release. Treat them as experimental; for serious plant / animal annotation, BRAKER or MAKER are the right tools.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
# Install tools and databases
myconote-cli install --yes
myconote-cli setup

# Annotate a fungal genome end-to-end
myconote-cli sort assembly.fa --min-length 500
myconote-cli mask assembly_sorted.fa --engine repeatmodeler --threads 8
myconote-cli predict assembly_masked.fa --kingdom fungi --locus-prefix MYORG
myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 --fasta assembly.fa \
    --trnascan --interproscan --email you@email.edu
myconote-cli submit annotate_out/annotated.gff3 --fasta assembly.fa \
    --organism "Genus species" --genetic-code 12  # table 12 for Candida CTG clade

# Optional: quantify RNA-seq expression against the annotation
myconote-cli convert annotated.gff3 --to cds --fasta assembly.fa -o cds.fa
myconote-cli fetch-rna SRR12345678 SRR12345679 -o rna/
myconote-cli quant cds.fa --samples rna/samples.tsv --genome assembly.fa
myconote-cli de-template --quant-dir quant_out --design '~ condition' \
    --contrast 'condition,treated,control' -o analysis.R
Rscript analysis.R   # needs R + tximport + DESeq2 + apeglm installed

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Tested on Brettanomyces bruxellensis (12.9 Mb, 30 contigs):

Step Time Result sort <1s 30 contigs sorted predict (Augustus) ~3 min 5,218 genes annotate (MMseqs2) ~1.5 min 75% genes with product names annotate (Pfam/hmmsearch) ~7 min 85.6% genes with domains annotate (InterProScan) ~5 min (cached) 98.3% genes annotated NCBI validation <1s PASSED (0 errors)

Pfam uses hmmsearch instead of hmmscan for a ~6× speedup on large proteomes.

docs.title: MycoNote competitiveness roadmap
docs.text: Synthesis of a three-agent research effort (tool-engineering, ML/DL gene finders, community/forum mining) + the 14-genome 4-tool benchmark + verification of what each competitor arm actually ran. Internal planning doc: every external claim carries its source; mechanism-justified gains with no isolated fungal point estimate are marked "measure on our 14-genome set before any manuscript claim."

docs.title: 1. Diagnosis (verified, not inferred)
docs.text:
Benchmark headline (per-genome collapse, n=5): gene F1 loose — BRAKER3 0.930 > funannotate 0.914 > MAKER 0.906 > MycoNote 0.899; strict — BRAKER 0.659 > funannotate 0.636 > MAKER 0.625 > MycoNote 0.609.

Two facts reframe the whole problem:

  • The gap is small and it's a strict-F1 (CDS-structure) problem, not loose. Loose: −1.5 pts vs funannotate, −3.1 vs BRAKER. Strict: −5.0 vs BRAKER. The priority is CDS-structure correctness / precision, not gene detection.
  • No tool used RNA-seq (verified in the wrappers). BRAKER3 ran protein-only (OrthoDB Fungi, --prot_seq); funannotate ran BUSCO-seed per-genome Augustus training; MAKER ran pure ab-initio (keep_preds=1); MycoNote ran pure ab-initio consensus (Augustus 3.3.3 + SNAP + GeneMark-ES, agreement-weighted). So BRAKER3's famous ~+20 transcript-F1 RNA-seq lift is not in play here — the gap MycoNote must close is the 1.5–5 pt structural gap, not 20 pts.

Where each competitor's edge comes from, given what they ran: - vs BRAKER3 → protein evidence (OrthoDB) + TSEBRA transcript selection. - vs funannotate → per-genome Augustus training (BUSCO-seeded) + EVM weighted consensus (not flat agreement). - vs MAKER (also pure ab-initio, yet 0.906 > 0.899) → MycoNote's 3-way consensus isn't currently buying accuracy over one well-configured Augustus.

The fungal ceiling caveat (most important for triage): in compact, intron-poor fungal genomes the ab-initio ceiling is already high, so evidence-integration pays far less than in vertebrates. GeneMark-EP+ lifted sensitivity on N. crassa (a fungus) by only ~2% even with the largest protein set, "because accuracy of GeneMark-ES was high as typical for fungal genomes" (GeneMark-EP+, NARGAB 2020). This is why MycoNote's --protein-hints A/B found no F1 lift (memory: accuracy_levers_closed) — it is consistent with the literature, largely the data, not just an integration bug.

docs.title: 2. Prioritized roadmap (ranked by accuracy-gain × feasibility × portability)
docs.text: Portability-safe, Rust/config-only changes are at the top by design — they preserve MycoNote's genuine edges (fastest prediction, best scaling, runs on any CPU without AVX2).

docs.title: #1 — Post-prediction filtering → raise strict F1 (do first; Rust-native, zero portability cost)
docs.text: Add a filter pass after the consensus: drop single-exon genes predicted purely ab-initio with no cross-predictor agreement; require complete ORFs (start+stop, no internal stop) unless flagged partial; drop single-predictor models below a length/score floor. Expose as --min-support / --keep-single-exon (deterministic). - Precedent: BRAKER3 explicitly removes single-exon purely-ab-initio genes to lift precision (BRAKER3, Genome Res 2024); MAKER's entire QC model is AED-based filtering (AED ≤0.5 "good", a good genome has >90% genes ≤0.5) (MAKER2, BMC Bioinformatics 2011). - Our AED analogue = the cross-predictor agreement we already compute. - Risk: filtering trades sensitivity for precision — tune on the 14 genomes and report F1, not precision alone.

docs.title: #2 — Upgrade the combiner: weighted vote + Augustus-HiQ tier (the mechanism funannotate beats us with)
docs.text: Generalize the combiner from "count agreement" to a weighted vote with a tunable per-predictor weight and a bonus tier for Augustus calls that agree with another predictor (our "high-quality Augustus" analogue). - funannotate runs EVidenceModeler with default weights Augustus=1, Augustus HiQ=2, GeneMark=1, snap=1 — it trusts (high-quality) Augustus more than the rest, and beats us on the same ab-initio inputs (funannotate predict docs; EVidenceModeler, Genome Biol 2008). - Do it Rust-native (keeps the pure-Rust/run-anywhere edge). Wrapping EVM v2 would match funannotate exactly but adds a Perl/bioconda dependency — only for a quick parity check. - Do NOT port TSEBRA for the ab-initio case — it scores transcripts by RNA-seq/protein support (ε/weight thresholds over evidence); with no evidence it degenerates (TSEBRA, BMC Bioinformatics 2021). TSEBRA is the right model for our RNA-seq mode, not this benchmark. - Gain is mechanism-justified (no isolated fungal point estimate) → measure first.

docs.title: #3 — Pfam annotate speed: confirm threading/chunking (we already use hmmsearch)
docs.text: MycoNote already prefers hmmsearch over hmmscan (src/annotate/pfam.rs), so the big hmmscan→hmmsearch I/O win (Eddy, cryptogenomicon) is already banked. The remaining lever is re-parallelization: hmmsearch leaves ~65% of work serial, and wrappers that re-chunk it (pyhmmer) cut a 97 h run to 27 h on 6 cores (PyHMMER, Bioinformatics 2023). Shard proteins across cores + tune --cpu/-Z. Zero portability cost. - Optional, flag-gated only: nail (Rust pHMM, ~26× HMMER, not SIMD-vectorized) (nail, PMC10862755) — but it requires MMseqs2 (a C++ binary), which erodes the pure-Rust/any-CPU edge. Keep hmmsearch the default; expose --pfam-backend {hmmsearch,nail} only if #3's free parallelization isn't enough.

docs.title: #4 — RNA-seq benchmark arm + repositioning (where the real accuracy lives)
docs.text: MycoNote already ships RNA-seq (v0.7.3); the benchmark just didn't use it. Add a second benchmark arm with RNA-seq so the paper isn't comparing MycoNote-ab-initio against tools in their evidence sweet spot, and reposition docs to "if you have reads, use them." The ~20-pt lift is an RNA-seq effect (BRAKER3). Harness work → bench-harness-engineer. No portability change.

docs.title: #5 — Tiberius as an optional benchmark-gated predictor (the one DL bet)
docs.text: For fungi, DL is not the obvious win it is for plants/vertebrates: Helixer only ties Augustus/GeneMark-ES on fungi (benchmark-only). Tiberius is the one worth testing — fungal ab-initio within ~3 pts of BRAKER3, dedicated fungal model (Tiberius multi-clade, PMC13142403). Integration shape has a precedent: funannotate2 runs Helixer standalone → takes its GFF3 → feeds EVM as high-weight evidence; same adapter pattern fits our combiner. - Portability cost: pulls in a TensorFlow stack (CPU wheels need AVX); no hard GPU requirement at fungal sizes but it dents the single-binary/any-CPU story → ship as --predictor tiberius, never a default. - Data-leakage guard: Tiberius/Helixer ship pretrained fungal models whose training species may overlap our panel — hold those genomes out when benchmarking.

docs.title: #6 — Document the known-nulls / hard limits (honesty, cheap)
docs.text:
• Protein hints give ~2% in fungi (ceiling above) → document as known-null; only revisit with evolutionarily-close proteins + confidence-tiered hints (miniprot + miniprothint, the GALBA recipe) and still expect low single digits (GALBA 2023; miniprot).
  • tmel (125 Mb) is a hard limit for all tools (~0.52–0.61 F1): >58% TEs + RIP (fungal C→T genome defense that destroys homology signal) (T. melanosporum genome; RIP). Frame it as a known-hard outlier — MycoNote collapses like the others, not worse.
  • Repeat-rich genomes need a de-novo RepeatModeler library + soft-mask (never hard-mask — it buries exons) (Galaxy masking). An adaptive filter (lenient for compact genomes, aggressive for Tuber-like) is funannotate's documented design (--repeat_filter off by default, on for high-repeat genomes).

docs.title: 3. Portability guardrails (the edges we must NOT trade away)
docs.text:
• Keep Augustus 3.3.3 the default (runs on any CPU). Competitors need AVX2-compiled 3.5.0. At most offer 3.5.0 as an opt-in fast path for AVX2 hosts.
  • Keep hmmsearch the portable Pfam default; nail/MMseqs2 behind a flag only.
  • Keep the combiner Rust-native (avoid EVM's Perl / Tiberius's TF as hard deps).

docs.title: 1 (filtering), #2-route-1 (weighted combiner), and #3 (hmmsearch parallelism)
docs.text: are all portability-neutral — which is exactly why they lead.

docs.title: 4. The honest positioning (for the paper)
docs.text: Not "faster" or "more accurate." The defensible story: competitive accuracy (within 1.5–5 F1 pts on ab-initio inputs), fastest prediction stage, best scaling to large genomes, runs on any CPU, complete one-tool pipeline to NCBI submission. The roadmap closes the strict-F1 gap with portability-safe changes first.

docs.title: 1 filtering + #3 hmmsearch parallelism — both free, portability-safe → implement, test on the 14 genomes.
2 Rust-native weighted combiner (Augustus-HiQ tier) — the funannotate mechanism, kept pure-Rust.
4 RNA-seq benchmark arm (bench-harness-engineer) — the honest accuracy story.
5 Tiberius optional, benchmark-gated with leakage holdout.
6 document the fungal protein-hint ceiling + the tmel hard limit.
Databases
docs.text:
MycoNote-CLI uses several external databases for functional annotation. Use myconote-cli setup to download and index them. Databases live in ~/.myconote/dbs by default.

myconote-cli setup --list                 # show all databases + download status
myconote-cli setup --dbs swiss-prot pfam  # download a specific set
myconote-cli setup --db augustus-fungi    # curated fungal Augustus species (~50) + the
                                          # species/generic/ self-training template
myconote-cli setup --dbs eggnog           # ~50 GB — only if you need COG/KEGG

docs.title: Database summary
docs.text: Database Size Used by Notes UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot ~250 MB MMseqs2 homology Curated protein annotations dbCAN ~50 MB CAZyme annotation Carbohydrate-active enzymes MEROPS ~80 MB Protease annotation Peptidase families Pfam ~350 MB Domain annotation (hmmsearch) Protein family HMMs GO ontology (go.obo) ~35 MB GO term mapping Gene Ontology eggNOG ~50 GB eggNOG-mapper Orthology + COG + KEGG. Download only if needed RepeatMasker libraries ~1 GB Repeat masking Downloaded by RepeatModeler2 during mask augustus-fungi ~small predict / train ~50 curated fungal species + the species/generic/ template needed for --augustus-training self Ollama + LLM model 4-48 GB explain (AI interpreter) Local LLM, auto-selected by RAM from pulled models. Setup: myconote-cli setup --dbs ollama Chat paper corpus ~50 MB explain (citations) Q1 open-access papers (CC-BY). Setup: myconote-cli setup --dbs chat-corpus

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text:
By default databases are stored in ~/.myconote/dbs. Override per-run with --db-dir <dir>.

myconote-cli setup --dbs swiss-prot pfam --db-dir /data/myconote_databases

docs.title: Checking database status
docs.text:
myconote-cli setup --list    # what is available and whether it's downloaded
myconote-cli setup --check   # verify existing databases are intact

Re-download anything with --force, or preview a download with --dry-run.

eggNOG database

The eggNOG database is ~50 GB compressed and needs ~50 GB more during indexing. Download it only if you need COG/KEGG assignments beyond what the Swiss-Prot (MMseqs2) + dbCAN annotations provide.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) or Linux (x86-64)
  • Miniconda or Anaconda
  • ~20 GB disk space for core tools; ~75 GB if downloading eggNOG databases

docs.title: Option A: Quick install (pre-built binary)
docs.text:
Download a pre-built binary for your platform. No Rust compiler needed.

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/K-nie/myconote-cli/main/quick-install.sh | bash

Then install external tools and databases: 

myconote-cli install --yes   # installs 30+ bioinformatics tools via conda
myconote-cli setup           # downloads annotation databases (~2.5 GB)

docs.title: Option B: Full installer (recommended for first-time setup)
docs.text:
Handles everything: Miniconda, Rust, binary build, tool installation, and database downloads.

git clone https://github.com/K-nie/myconote-cli.git
cd myconote-cli
bash install.sh

Estimated time: 20-40 minutes on first install.

docs.title: Option C: Docker
docs.text:
docker pull ghcr.io/k-nie/myconote-cli:latest
docker run -v $(pwd):/data myconote-cli predict /data/genome.fa --kingdom fungi

All tools and databases are pre-installed in the container.

docs.title: Option D: Singularity / Apptainer (HPC)
docs.text:
singularity pull myconote-cli.sif docker://ghcr.io/k-nie/myconote-cli:latest
singularity run myconote-cli.sif predict genome.fa --kingdom fungi

docs.title: Option E: Build from source
docs.text:
If you have Rust >= 1.74:

git clone https://github.com/K-nie/myconote-cli.git
cd myconote-cli
cargo build --release
cp target/release/myconote-cli ~/.local/bin/
myconote-cli install --yes
myconote-cli setup

docs.title: Verify installation
docs.text:
myconote-cli --version       # shows version and banner
myconote-cli check           # reports status of all 30+ external tools
myconote-cli setup --check   # shows database download status

docs.title: Database setup
docs.text:
myconote-cli setup                        # download all core databases
myconote-cli setup --db swiss-prot pfam   # download specific databases
myconote-cli setup --check                # verify what's installed

Core databases (~2.5 GB):

Database Size Used by Swiss-Prot (MMseqs2) ~1 GB annotate (product names) Pfam-A HMMs ~300 MB annotate (domain search) BUSCO lineages ~500 MB annotate (completeness) dbCAN (CAZyme) ~200 MB annotate --cazyme MEROPS ~100 MB annotate --merops

eggNOG database

The eggNOG database is ~50 GB and is NOT downloaded by default. Download only if you need COG/KEGG annotation: 

download_eggnog_data.py -y --data_dir ~/.eggnog_mapper/data

docs.title: Ollama setup (for explain AI interpreter)
docs.text:
The explain command uses a local LLM via Ollama for privacy-first result interpretation. No data leaves your machine.

myconote-cli setup ollama        # install Ollama, detect RAM, pull best model

This will:

  1. Install Ollama (latest version from GitHub releases)
  2. Start the Ollama server
  3. Auto-detect your system RAM and select the most capable model
  4. Pull and verify the model

Available model tiers:

RAM Model Quality 48+ GB llama3.3:70b-instruct-q4_K_M Best 24+ GB qwen2.5:32b-instruct-q4_K_M Excellent 16+ GB mistral-small:22b Strong 12+ GB qwen2.5:14b Good 8+ GB llama3.1:8b Baseline

Override with MYCONOTE_CHAT_MODEL=<model> or --model <model> on the explain command.

Optionally download Q1 open-access papers for grounded citations:

myconote-cli setup chat-corpus   # ~50 MB, CC-BY licensed papers only

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
After installation:

myconote-cli learn    # interactive tutorial (22 lessons, ~4 hours)

Or jump straight to the Quick Start guide.

docs.title: Interactive Tutorial (myconote-cli learn)
docs.text: Learn myconote-cli step by step, right in your terminal. Inspired by R's swirl package — no browser needed, no external tools required.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
myconote-cli learn          # list all lessons and your progress
myconote-cli learn 1        # start lesson 1
myconote-cli learn basics   # start a lesson by name
myconote-cli learn --resume # pick up where you left off
myconote-cli learn --reset  # clear all progress

Aliases also work: myconote-cli tutorial or myconote-cli swirl

docs.title: Available Lessons
docs.text: The catalogue is split into four tracks. Lessons within each track can be completed in any order, but new users should walk the foundation track first.

docs.title: Foundation track (run in order if you're new)
docs.text: # Lesson Duration Topics 1 Welcome to MycoNote ~12 min Pipeline overview, kingdoms, file formats, key concepts 2 Setup & Installation ~10 min install, setup, check, species commands 3 Pre-processing: Sort & Mask ~10 min sort, masking engines, soft vs hard masking 4 Gene Prediction ~14 min Augustus, SNAP, agreement-weighted consensus, protein evidence, ploidy, weights 5 Functional Annotation ~15 min Swiss-Prot, Pfam, BUSCO, tRNA, genetic codes, InterProScan 6 Advanced: Training & Evidence ~12 min RNA-seq training, Trinity, PASA, custom evidence weights 7 NCBI Submission ~10 min GFF3 validation, .tbl generation, table2asn, BioProject 8 Stats, Comparative Genomics, and Conversion ~12 min stats, compare, convert, handoff to Proksee/IGV/clinker

docs.title: RNA-seq track (lessons 9-14, completable in any order)
docs.text: # Lesson Duration Topics 9 RNA-seq Quantification (quant) ~12 min salmon decoy-aware index, fastp QC, tximport-ready outputs, SHA256 cache 10 SRA/ENA Download (fetch-rna) ~10 min ENA REST default, sra-toolkit fallback, MD5 verification, sample-sheet emission 11 Differential Expression (de-template) ~12 min tximport + DESeq2 + apeglm template, design formulas, contrasts 12 Allele-Specific Expression (ase) ~14 min Phased VCF + personalized transcriptome, unphased-het hard error, asymmetry detection 13 ASE Binomial Test (ase-template) ~10 min Per-sample-corrected null, informativeness filter, base-R only 14 GO Enrichment (go-template) ~10 min topGO Fisher's exact test, BP/MF/CC, BH within ontology, dot plot

docs.title: Modern predictors track (lessons 15-16)
docs.text: # Lesson Duration Topics 15 BRAKER for Maximum Accuracy ~10 min predict --use-braker, BRAKER1/2/3 mode auto-detection, conflict guard 16 GeneMark Variants (--genemark-mode) ~10 min ES/ET/EP+/ETP+, ProtHint, when each is appropriate

docs.title: Quality and reproducibility track (lessons 17-20)
docs.text: # Lesson Duration Topics 17 Contig Dedup (clean --mode contigs) ~8 min minimap2 self-alignment, coverage/identity thresholds, deterministic ties 18 Augustus Fungal Species Bundle ~8 min The 49-species manifest, AUGUSTUS_CONFIG_PATH, retrain vs bundled 19 Reproducibility Manifests ~8 min quant_bundle.json / ase_bundle.json, SHA256 hashing, byte-identical re-runs 20 NCBI Codon Tables (Candida CTG focus) ~12 min 25 NCBI tables, Table 12, silent-mistranslation failure mode

docs.title: Evidence and training track (lessons 21-22)
docs.text:
# Lesson Duration Topics 21 Protein Hints: miniprot Evidence ~10 min predict --protein-hints, the diamond prefilter, --protein-hints-min-identity (close relatives beat remote proteins) 22 Self-Training Augustus Models ~10 min predict --augustus-training self, prerequisites (companion scripts + species/generic/), why stock usually wins

Total: ~237 minutes (~4 hours) covering the full pipeline plus modern features added since v0.5.

docs.title: During a Lesson
docs.text:
Type your answer and press Enter. Special commands:

Command What it does hint Get a contextual hint for the current question info Peek at the expected answer skip Move to the next question without answering quit / bye Save progress and exit

After 3 wrong attempts, the correct answer is revealed automatically — the goal is learning, not testing.

docs.title: Question Types
docs.text:
The tutorial uses 5 question types:

Multiple choice — pick a, b, c, or d 

  Which tool does myconote-cli use for protein homology search?
    a) BLAST
    b) MMseqs2
    c) DIAMOND
    d) HMMER

  > b
  Correct!

Free text — type the answer (fuzzy-matched, typos forgiven) 

  What command installs all missing external tools?

  > install
  Correct!

True/False 

  True or False: myconote-cli is focused primarily on fungal genomes.

  > true
  Correct! Defaults, benchmarks, and the test fixtures are all tuned
  for fungal annotation. The `--kingdom` flag accepts plant/animal/
  insect/protist too, but those paths are experimental and not
  validated on large genomes.

Fill-in-the-blank — complete a command template 

  Complete the command:
  myconote-cli ___ genes.gff3 --to gtf

  > convert
  Correct!

Order steps — arrange pipeline stages correctly 

  Put these steps in the correct pipeline order:
    1) annotate
    2) predict
    3) mask
    4) sort

  > 4,3,2,1
  Correct! sort -> mask -> predict -> annotate

docs.title: Progress Tracking
docs.text:
Your progress is saved to ~/.myconote/learn_progress.json and persists between sessions.

  • Completed lessons show a green checkmark in the lesson list
  • --resume picks up exactly where you left off
  • --reset clears all progress to start fresh

docs.title: For Workshop Instructors
docs.text:
The learn system can be used in a classroom setting:

  1. Students install myconote-cli on their laptops
  2. Each student works through lessons at their own pace
  3. No internet required (all lessons are built into the binary)
  4. Progress is per-user, so students can resume between sessions

For a longer workshop format, see the Workshop Lesson page which provides a 3-hour instructor-guided curriculum.

docs.title: Lesson Overview
docs.text:
Duration: ~3 hours (self-paced) or one half-day workshop

Software required: Myconote_CLI, conda, a Unix terminal (macOS or Linux)

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

  1. Explain the stages of a fungal genome annotation pipeline
  2. Install and verify Myconote_CLI and its external tool dependencies
  3. Run each pipeline step — sort, mask, predict, and annotate — on a real genome
  4. Interpret annotation statistics and quality metrics
  5. Export to standard formats and hand off to downstream tools (Proksee, IGV, clinker)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Basic command-line navigation (cd, ls, mkdir)
  • Familiarity with FASTA and GFF3 file formats
  • A conda installation (Miniconda or Anaconda)

docs.title: Episode 1: Setting Up
docs.text: Time: ~30 minutes

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Genome annotation is the process of identifying the locations and functions of genes in a DNA sequence. A typical fungal annotation pipeline involves four core stages:

  1. Repeat masking — identifying repetitive elements so they do not confuse gene predictors
  2. Gene prediction — using statistical models to find gene structures (exons, introns, UTRs)
  3. Evidence integration — combining predictions from multiple tools using evidence weights
  4. Functional annotation — assigning biological functions to predicted proteins

Myconote_CLI wraps all of these stages into a single tool with consistent interfaces and standard output formats.

docs.title: Installing Myconote_CLI
docs.text:
There are three ways to install Myconote_CLI. Option C is recommended for most users.

Option A: One-shot installer

Runs everything automatically — Rust, conda environment, tools, and databases:

git clone https://github.com/K-nie/myconote-cli
cd myconote-cli
bash install.sh

Option B: Manual installation

For users who want control over each step:

conda create -n myconote python=3.10
conda activate myconote
cargo build --release
myconote-cli install --yes

Option C: Use a pre-built release (recommended)

Download the pre-compiled binary directly — no Rust compiler needed:

# macOS (Apple Silicon)
curl -L https://github.com/K-nie/myconote-cli/releases/latest/download/myconote-cli-aarch64-apple-darwin \
    -o myconote-cli && chmod +x myconote-cli

# Linux (x86-64)
curl -L https://github.com/K-nie/myconote-cli/releases/latest/download/myconote-cli-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu \
    -o myconote-cli && chmod +x myconote-cli

I recommend Option C because it gives you a clean starting point without requiring a Rust toolchain, and it is always the latest tested release.

docs.title: Verifying the installation
docs.text:
myconote-cli --version

You should see the banner and version number. Then run the tool checker:

myconote-cli check

This reports the install status of all 27 external tools. A typical new installation will show most tools as installed via conda, with SignalP and GeneMark flagged as requiring manual download.

Key point: You do not need every tool installed to run the pipeline. Myconote will skip steps where the required tool is missing and tell you what to install.

docs.title: Challenge 1.1
docs.text:
Run myconote-cli check and identify:

  1. How many tools are installed?
  2. Which tools are listed as MISSING?
  3. What command does the output suggest for installing missing tools?

docs.title: Episode 2: Preparing Your Genome
docs.text: Time: ~20 minutes

docs.title: Why we sort contigs first
docs.text:
Most genome assemblers output contigs in arbitrary order with long, non-informative headers like NODE_1_length_2474448_cov_85.2. The sort command:

  • Orders contigs from longest to shortest (annotation tools perform best on long contigs)
  • Filters out very short contigs that add noise without contributing gene models
  • Preserves your original contig names by default (lossless)
  • Optionally renames headers to clean sequential IDs (scaffold_1, scaffold_2, …) with --ncbi-clean, and saves a rename table so you can trace back to the originals

docs.title: Running sort
docs.text:
# NCBI-ready: rename to scaffold_N and keep the lift-over table
myconote-cli sort genome.fa \
    --ncbi-clean --prefix scaffold \
    --min-length 1000 \
    --rename-table rename_table.tsv \
    -o sorted.fa

The output includes a summary:

Sorting genome: genome.fa
  Contigs kept:   30
  Total assembly: 13.2 Mbp
  Longest contig: 2.47 Mbp
  Shortest kept:  1,024 bp
  Output:         sorted.fa
  Rename table:   rename_table.tsv

Key point: Always run sort before masking. Consistent, clean headers prevent errors in downstream tools that parse sequence IDs from GFF3 and FASTA files together.

docs.title: Challenge 2.1
docs.text:
Sort the practice genome, then answer:

myconote-cli sort tests/data/candida_tropicalis.fas \
    --min-length 10000 --ncbi-clean \
    -o ct_sorted.fa
  1. How many contigs passed the 10,000 bp filter?
  2. What fraction of the total assembly length do they represent?
  3. With --ncbi-clean, what would the first contig header look like in ct_sorted.fa? (And what would it be without that flag?)

docs.title: Episode 3: Repeat Masking
docs.text: Time: ~30 minutes (runtime varies with genome size)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Eukaryotic genomes contain 20–80% repetitive elements (transposons, tandem repeats, satellites). Gene predictors trained on unmasked genomes frequently predict false genes inside repeat regions. Soft-masking converts repeat nucleotides to lowercase letters — gene predictors can see the sequence context but are trained to ignore lowercase regions.

Myconote supports two masking engines:

Engine Approach When to use repeatmasker Uses a pre-built repeat library (Dfam) Fast; works well for well-studied organisms repeatmodeler Builds a custom repeat library de novo Slower but more accurate for novel genomes

Option A: RepeatMasker with Dfam library

myconote-cli mask sorted.fa \
    --engine repeatmasker \
    --species fungi \
    --threads 8

Option B: RepeatModeler + RepeatMasker (recommended for novel genomes)

myconote-cli mask sorted.fa \
    --engine repeatmodeler \
    --threads 16

I recommend Option B for any genome not closely related to a reference assembly in Dfam, because it builds a repeat library tailored to your specific organism.

The output is sorted.fa.masked — identical to the input but with repeat regions in lowercase.

docs.title: Challenge 3.1
docs.text:
After masking, calculate the repeat content:

# Count lowercase (masked) bases
python3 -c "
seq = open('sorted.fa.masked').read()
seq = ''.join(seq.split()[1::2] if '>' in seq else [seq])
total = sum(1 for c in seq if c.isalpha())
masked = sum(1 for c in seq if c.islower())
print(f'Masked: {masked/total*100:.1f}%')
"

What percentage of your genome was masked? Is this typical for a fungal genome?

Hint: Most ascomycete fungi have 2–10% repeat content; basidiomycetes can have up to 40%.

docs.title: Episode 4: Gene Prediction
docs.text: Time: ~45 minutes

docs.title: How multi-tool prediction works
docs.text:
Myconote runs up to four ab initio gene predictors and combines their predictions with its own agreement-weighted consensus — an EVM-inspired weighted-evidence scheme that does not invoke the external EvidenceModeler tool. Each predictor is assigned a weight based on its reliability for the target kingdom:

Predictor Approach Default weight (fungi) Augustus Generalised HMM 6 SNAP Hidden Markov Model 2 GlimmerHMM Generalised HMM 2 GeneMark-ES Self-training HMM 4

MycoNote's agreement-weighted consensus merge produces a gene set that is generally more accurate than any single predictor alone.

docs.title: Running predict
docs.text:
myconote-cli predict sorted.fa.masked \
    --kingdom fungi \
    --glimmerhmm \
    --threads 8 \
    --output predict_out/

Augustus and SNAP run by default; add --glimmerhmm and/or --genemark-mode to bring in more predictors, or --no-snap to drop one. Key options:

  • --kingdom — sets the default Augustus species model and BUSCO lineage
  • --clade saccharomycotina|pezizomycotina|basidiomycota — pick a clade-appropriate fungal default instead of S288C
  • --species — override the Augustus species model (default: saccharomyces_cerevisiae_S288C)
  • --protein-hints <proteins.fa> — add protein evidence (miniprot → Augustus hints); see predict --help for the identity gate

docs.title: Choosing an Augustus species model
docs.text:
The default species model for fungi is saccharomyces_cerevisiae_S288C. If your organism is more closely related to a different well-studied fungus, override the default:

# For a filamentous ascomycete
myconote-cli predict sorted.fa.masked \
    --kingdom fungi \
    --species aspergillus_fumigatus \
    --threads 8

# See all available models
myconote-cli species --grouped

docs.title: Challenge 4.1
docs.text:
Run prediction on the practice genome and examine the output:

myconote-cli predict tests/data/candida_tropicalis.fas.masked \
    --kingdom fungi --threads 4 --output ct_predict/

Then check the gene statistics:

myconote-cli stats ct_predict/consensus.gff3
  1. How many genes were predicted?
  2. What is the mean gene length?
  3. How does this compare to the reference annotation (6,290 genes)?

docs.title: Episode 5: Functional Annotation
docs.text: Time: ~40 minutes

docs.title: What functional annotation does
docs.text:
Gene prediction gives you where genes are. Functional annotation tells you what they do by comparing predicted proteins against curated databases:

annotate takes the gene GFF3 as a positional argument and the genome via --fasta. The core sources run by default (MMseqs2, Pfam, BUSCO); the rest are opt-in with the flag shown:

Source Flag Provides MMseqs2 default on Gene names, species of best hit Pfam default on (--no-pfam) Protein domain families BUSCO default on (--no-busco) Completeness assessment EggNOG --eggnog GO terms, KEGG pathways, COG categories CAZyme --cazyme Carbohydrate-active enzyme families MEROPS --merops Protease families antiSMASH --antismash Secondary metabolite gene clusters

docs.title: Running annotate
docs.text:
Option A: Core annotation (default, fast)

myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 \
    --fasta sorted.fa.masked \
    --threads 8 \
    --output annotation/

Option B: Full annotation (recommended for publication)

myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 \
    --fasta sorted.fa.masked \
    --eggnog --cazyme --merops --antismash --secretome --trnascan \
    --threads 8 \
    --output annotation/

Option B adds GO terms, KEGG pathways, and secondary-metabolite clusters expected in most fungal genome papers. Since v0.7.8 the EggNOG step runs ~4× faster (--dmnd_iterate no by default); pass --eggnog-iterate to restore the slower, maximum-recall path.

Note: Option B requires the eggNOG database (~50 GB). If it is not yet downloaded, Myconote will skip the --eggnog step and warn you.

docs.title: Challenge 5.1
docs.text:
After annotation, examine the functional coverage:

myconote-cli stats annotation/annotated.gff3 --format json | python3 -c "
import json, sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
print('Total genes:', d['gene_count'])
print('Annotated (any function):', d.get('annotated_count', 'N/A'))
"

What percentage of predicted genes received at least one functional annotation? What does a low percentage suggest about the organism's novelty?

docs.title: Episode 6: Visualising Results
docs.text:
Time: ~20 minutes

MycoNote does not ship its own plotting or browser — the built-in versions were removed in v0.2.0 because established tools already do this better. Instead, export your annotation and hand off to:

  • Proksee (web, https://proksee.ca/) — publication-quality circular genome maps. Upload the .gbk from convert --to genbank.
  • IGV (desktop) — drop the GFF3 + FASTA for interactive browsing.
  • clinker (pip install clinker) — cross-species gene-cluster synteny ribbons from multiple .gbk files.

docs.title: Convert once, use everywhere
docs.text:
myconote-cli convert annotation/annotated.gff3 \
    --to genbank \
    --fasta sorted.fa \
    -o final.gbk

# Upload final.gbk to Proksee for a circular map, or:
clinker final.gbk other_species.gbk -o synteny.html

docs.title: Converting to other formats
docs.text:
# For R/Python analysis
myconote-cli convert annotation/annotated.gff3 --to table -o genes.tsv

# For Geneious / SnapGene
myconote-cli convert annotation/annotated.gff3 --to genbank \
    --fasta sorted.fa -o annotation.gbk

# Protein sequences for BLAST or OrthoFinder
myconote-cli convert annotation/annotated.gff3 --to protein -o proteins.faa

docs.title: Key Points
docs.text:
• Run pipeline steps in order: sort → mask → (train) → predict → update → annotate
  • Use --kingdom fungi for fungal genomes; this sets correct defaults for all downstream steps
  • myconote-cli check tells you exactly which tools are installed before you start
  • All outputs use standard formats (GFF3, FASTA, GenBank) compatible with other tools
  • The stats command gives you a quality summary at any point in the pipeline
  • eggNOG functional annotation is optional but strongly recommended for publication
  • Two tools (SignalP 6, GeneMark-ES) require manual download due to licensing

docs.text: Since the initial workshop lesson was written, myconote-cli has gained several major features:

docs.title: Instructor Notes
docs.text:
Episode 1 (Setup): Allow extra time — conda environment creation and Rust compilation can take 5–10 minutes on first run. Pre-build the binary ahead of time for a classroom setting.

Episode 3 (Masking): RepeatModeler on a 13 Mbp fungal genome takes ~1–2 hours. For a workshop, pre-run masking and provide the .masked file so participants start from Episode 4.

Episode 4 (Prediction): Full consensus prediction on 13 Mbp takes ~30–60 minutes depending on threads. Same advice — provide pre-computed output for time-constrained workshops.

Episode 5 (Annotation): Without eggNOG (~50 GB), annotation runs in ~15 minutes. The --pfam --busco flags alone are sufficient for the challenges.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Annotate a fungal genome from start to finish. Estimated time: 30-60 minutes (excluding database downloads).

New to myconote-cli? Run myconote-cli learn for an interactive tutorial that teaches each concept step by step.

docs.title: 1. Verify your installation
docs.text:
myconote-cli --version       # check binary is installed
myconote-cli check           # verify external tools
myconote-cli setup --check   # verify databases

If tools or databases are missing: 

myconote-cli install --yes   # install all missing tools via conda
myconote-cli setup           # download all databases (~2.5 GB)

docs.title: 2. Sort and length-filter contigs
docs.text:
myconote-cli sort assembly.fa --min-length 500

Reorders contigs longest-first and drops short ones. Lossless by default — your original contig names pass through unchanged. For an NCBI submission, add --ncbi-clean (optionally --rename-table rename.tsv) to rename to scaffold_1, scaffold_2, … and record the lift-over map.

docs.title: 3. Mask repeats
docs.text:
myconote-cli mask assembly_sorted.fa --engine repeatmodeler --threads 8

Builds a de novo repeat library with RepeatModeler2, then soft-masks the genome with RepeatMasker. Soft-masked bases are lowercased so gene finders can skip them.

docs.title: 4. Train gene predictors (optional)
docs.text:
If you have RNA-seq data:

myconote-cli train assembly_masked.fa \
  --left R1.fastq.gz --right R2.fastq.gz \
  --species my_organism --threads 8

This assembles transcripts with Trinity, aligns them with minimap2, builds a PASA database, and trains Augustus + SNAP on your organism's gene structures.

Tip

If you don't have RNA-seq, skip this step. Augustus will use its pre-trained model for your kingdom.

docs.title: 5. Predict gene models
docs.text:
myconote-cli predict assembly_masked.fa \
  --kingdom fungi \
  --locus-prefix MYORG \
  --threads 8

Runs Augustus + SNAP (+ GeneMark when configured), merges predictions with MycoNote's agreement-weighted consensus, and writes a clean consensus.gff3 with sequential locus tags.

Advanced options: 

# Clade-appropriate Augustus model (instead of the S288C default off-Saccharomycotina)
myconote-cli predict assembly_masked.fa --kingdom fungi --clade basidiomycota

# Add protein hints (miniprot → Augustus), keeping only close relatives
myconote-cli predict assembly_masked.fa --kingdom fungi \
  --protein-hints orthodb_fungi.fa --protein-hints-min-identity 70

# Feed a protein DB to GeneMark EP+/ETP+ (ProtHint), not standalone hints
myconote-cli predict assembly_masked.fa --kingdom fungi \
  --genemark-mode ep --protein-fasta swissprot.fasta --locus-prefix MYORG

# Handle diploid/polyploid genomes
myconote-cli predict assembly_masked.fa --ploidy 2

docs.title: 6. Functional annotation
docs.text:
myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 \
  --fasta assembly_masked.fa \
  --kingdom fungi \
  --trnascan \
  --threads 8

Runs MMseqs2 (Swiss-Prot homology), Pfam (domain search via hmmsearch), BUSCO (completeness), GO terms, and tRNAscan-SE (tRNA genes).

Enable additional annotation sources: 

myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 \
  --fasta assembly_masked.fa \
  --eggnog --cazyme --secretome --antismash --merops \
  --interproscan --email you@email.edu \
  --genetic-code 12    # for Candida CTG clade

EggNog is off by default — run with or without it: 

# fast (default): Swiss-Prot + Pfam + CAZyme + MEROPS, no emapper
myconote-cli annotate ... --cazyme --merops

# full: add EggNog orthology (COG/NOG/KEGG). Adds a ~30-min emapper step;
# it does not change gene-model accuracy, only functional coverage.
myconote-cli annotate ... --cazyme --merops --eggnog --eggnog-db <dir>
--eggnog turns the emapper layer on; --no-eggnog (the default) is the explicit off-switch. If both are given, the last one wins.

docs.title: 7. Validate and prepare NCBI submission
docs.text:
# Check for errors first
myconote-cli submit annotate_out/annotated.gff3 \
  --fasta assembly_masked.fa \
  --organism "Genus species" --validate-only

# Generate submission files
myconote-cli submit annotate_out/annotated.gff3 \
  --fasta assembly_masked.fa \
  --organism "Genus species" \
  --strain "CBS 123" \
  --locus-prefix MYORG \
  --bioproject PRJNA123456

docs.title: 8. Explore your results
docs.text:
# Summary statistics with taxonomic benchmarking
myconote-cli stats annotate_out/annotated.gff3 --taxon fungi

# Convert to GenBank for Proksee upload or IGV browsing
myconote-cli convert annotate_out/annotated.gff3 --to genbank --fasta assembly_masked.fa

# For interactive exploration, load the GFF3 + FASTA in IGV (desktop)
# or upload the .gbk to Proksee (https://proksee.ca/) for publication maps.
# For cross-species gene-cluster synteny, pipe multiple .gbk files into clinker.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: File Description predict_out/consensus.gff3 Predicted gene models annotate_out/annotated.gff3 Gene models with functional annotations annotate_out/proteins.fa Predicted protein sequences annotate_out/annotations.tsv Full annotation table (for R/Python) annotate_out/annotation_report.txt Summary with gene counts and coverage submit_out/annotation.tbl NCBI feature table

docs.title: 9. Interpret your results with AI
docs.text:
# Interpret prediction results (local LLM, no data leaves your machine)
myconote-cli explain predict

# Rules-only mode (no Ollama needed)
myconote-cli explain predict --no-llm

# Analyze a pasted error
echo "ERROR: SEQ_FEAT.NoStop" | myconote-cli explain --paste

First-time setup for the AI interpreter:

myconote-cli setup ollama        # install Ollama + best model for your hardware
myconote-cli setup chat-corpus   # optional: Q1 paper corpus for grounded citations

docs.title: 10. Annotate multiple genomes at once
docs.text:
# From a directory of FASTAs
myconote-cli batch genomes/ --kingdom fungi --threads 8

# From a sample sheet with per-genome settings
myconote-cli batch samples.tsv --parallel 4

# Generate HTCondor submit files for HPC
myconote-cli batch genomes/ --condor --condor-mem 64G

docs.title: myconote ase-template
docs.text:
Generate a ready-to-run R script that performs a binomial exact test for allele-specific expression on myconote-cli ase output. The tool writes the script; you run it with Rscript.

Companion to ase — same design philosophy as de-template (write R, user runs R, no R runtime inside MycoNote-CLI). The statistics are simple enough that we don't need Bioconductor: base R's binom.test() + p.adjust() covers it.

docs.title: Prerequisites — install before running the emitted script
docs.text:
Base R ≥ 4.0. Nothing else.

No DESeq2, no tximport, no BiocManager::install. The emitted script uses only read.table, binom.test, p.adjust, and hist.

Verify you have R:

Rscript --version

If Rscript isn't on your PATH, the tool warns but still writes the script — you can run it on another host.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Run it on the output of myconote-cli ase:

myconote-cli ase-template --ase-dir ase_out -o ase_analysis.R
Rscript ase_analysis.R

--ase-dir is shorthand for --counts ase_out/ase_counts.tsv --summary ase_out/ase_summary.tsv.

You get two output files:

  • ase_results.tsv — long-format table: one row per transcript × sample with pvalue, BH-adjusted padj, hap0_frac, imbalance, and a reason field telling you why a row was skipped (e.g. below --min-reads).
  • ase_imbalance.pdf — per-sample histogram of hap0-fraction, with a dashed red line at that sample's null proportion.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: flag meaning --ase-dir <dir> Shortcut: fills --counts and --summary from their canonical positions inside the ase output directory. --counts <ase_counts.tsv> Explicit path to the counts matrix from ase. Required if --ase-dir isn't given. --summary <ase_summary.tsv> Optional; enables filtering to informative transcripts. Falling through without it still works but tests every transcript. --output <file.R> / -o Output R script (default ase_analysis.R). --haplotype-names N1,N2 Must match what ase used (default hap0,hap1). --fdr <n> BH significance threshold (default 0.05). --min-reads <n> Skip (transcript × sample) pairs with total read count below this (default 20). Below this the binomial test is uninformative — too few reads to resolve small departures from the null. --include-uninformative Test every transcript even when ase_summary.tsv marks them as uninformative (haplotype sequences identical). Off by default.

docs.title: The binomial test
docs.text:
For each transcript × sample pair, the script runs:

binom.test(hap0_count, hap0_count + hap1_count, p = null_p0[sample])

The null proportion null_p0[sample] is sample-specific, computed as:

null_p0[s] = sum(hap0 counts for sample s across all transcripts) /
             sum(total counts for sample s across all transcripts)

This is the key correction: if sample 1 maps 52 % of its reads to hap0 globally (e.g. because hap0 has better-quality assembly), the null is 0.52 for that sample, not 0.5. Without this correction, every transcript in sample 1 would appear to show ASE toward hap0.

BH adjustment (p.adjust(..., method = "BH")) is applied per sample, not pooled. Each sample is its own independent experiment.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Two filters run in order:

  1. Informative filter (on by default, requires --summary): drops transcripts where both haplotypes have identical CDS sequence. Can't test what can't differ.
  2. Min-reads filter (per-row): if hap0_count + hap1_count < --min-reads for a given (transcript, sample) pair, the row is kept in the output with reason = "below_min_reads" and pvalue = NA. It does not contribute to BH adjustment.

docs.title: What's in the emitted R script
docs.text:
Hand-maintained template. Structure:

# Header with generation metadata
# Inputs block (edit here to re-run with different params)
# Load ase_counts.tsv
# Filter to informative transcripts if ASE_SUMMARY is set
# Parse <sample>.<hap> column names (splits on the LAST dot, so sample IDs can contain dots)
# Verify both haplotypes are present for every sample
# Compute per-sample null_p0
# Per-transcript-per-sample binom.test loop
# BH adjustment within each sample
# Write ase_results.tsv
# Per-sample imbalance histogram PDF
# sessionInfo() for reproducibility

Every substitution is a named R variable at the top (ASE_COUNTS, HAP_NAMES, FDR_CUTOFF, MIN_READS_PER_SAMPLE, FILTER_UNINFORMATIVE). Edit and re-run without regenerating.

docs.title: Reading ase_results.tsv
docs.text:
column meaning transcript Transcript ID from ase_counts.tsv. sample Sample ID. hap0_count, hap1_count Raw counts. Fractional (salmon's estimated counts) preserved. total hap0_count + hap1_count. hap0_frac hap0_count / total. imbalance hap0_frac − null_p0[sample]. Signed: positive = excess hap0 expression, negative = excess hap1. null_p This sample's null hap0 proportion. pvalue Two-sided binomial exact test p-value. NA when total < MIN_READS_PER_SAMPLE. padj BH-adjusted p-value within this sample. NA for skipped rows. reason "tested" or "below_min_reads". significant padj < FDR_CUTOFF. FALSE for NA rows.

Sort by (sample, padj) in R or shell — the script writes in transcript × sample order so you can join it back to other tables cleanly.

docs.title: What ase-template does NOT do
docs.text:
• Doesn't run the test. The tool writes the script. You run Rscript ase_analysis.R.
  • Doesn't do cis/trans regression. For that, look at [Wittkopp et al. 2004 / Landry et al. 2005]-style per-transcript linear models — the emitted script is the first pass; keep the output of ase_counts.tsv around and model it yourself if you need cis/trans decomposition.
  • Doesn't handle >2 haplotypes. Binomial testing on pairs only. Polyploid ASE (e.g. triploid) needs a multinomial / Dirichlet-multinomial formulation — out of scope for 0.5.0.
  • Doesn't do gene-level aggregation. Operates at the transcript level, matching salmon's output. Summing isoforms by gene changes the null (Simpson's paradox territory); do it deliberately, not by default.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Haplotype labels in ase_counts.tsv (hap0,hap1) don't match --haplotype-names (paternal,maternal)" — you passed custom --haplotype-names to ase but the default to ase-template, or vice versa. They must match.
  • "Sample 'X' is missing one or both haplotype columns" — the counts matrix was hand-edited, or an earlier salmon run failed partway. Re-run ase to regenerate.
  • All pvalue are NA — --min-reads is higher than your per-transcript totals. Lower it (e.g. --min-reads 5) for a smoke test, but don't over-interpret: the binomial test is weak at small N.
  • null_p0[sample] looks extreme (e.g. 0.8) — one haplotype dominates global mapping. Check the asymmetry_flag column in ase_bundle.json from the ase run; if flagged, fix the phasing or assembly before trusting any per-transcript result.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• myconote-cli ase — produces the ase_counts.tsv + ase_summary.tsv this script consumes.
  • myconote-cli de-template — same "emit R, user runs R" pattern for DESeq2 differential expression.
  • Binomial exact test background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_test
  • BH (Benjamini–Hochberg) FDR: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_discovery_rate

docs.title: myconote ase
docs.text:
Quantify allele-specific expression (ASE) in heterozygous, hybrid, or polyploid fungal genomes. Builds personalized transcriptomes per haplotype from a phased VCF, then runs salmon independently against each haplotype so each read is assigned to the allele it matches better.

ASE is the rule, not the exception, for many fungi: diploid Candida isolates, Saccharomyces F1 hybrids, interspecies crosses, and polyploids all need this. Quantifying against a single reference under-counts the allele farther from reference — reference bias — and makes real cis-regulatory differences invisible.

docs.title: What this does
docs.text:
1. Parses a phased VCF. Unphased heterozygous sites error out with a line number — ASE requires phasing; we refuse to guess.
  2. For each haplotype, applies its variants to the reference CDS to produce a personalized transcriptome FASTA.
  3. Runs fastp on each sample once (QC is haplotype-independent), then salmon against each haplotype's index. Two salmon runs per sample.
  4. Merges per-sample, per-haplotype quant.sf into a transcript × <sample>.<hap> counts matrix.
  5. Computes a per-transcript informative flag (haplotypes actually differ in CDS sequence), per-haplotype variant counts, and a max mapping-rate asymmetry across samples.
  6. Writes a reproducibility bundle (ase_bundle.json) with SHA256s of every input, tool versions, variant-application counts, and per-sample mapping rates.

docs.title: Prerequisites — install before running
docs.text:
You need salmon and fastp on your PATH:

conda install -c bioconda salmon fastp

Then prepare inputs:

  1. Reference CDS FASTA (cds.fa) — from myconote-cli convert --to cds genome.fa annotated.gff3.
  2. Phased VCF (phased.vcf.gz) — produced by your own variant-calling pipeline (GATK HaplotypeCaller → WhatsHap, or HapCUT2, or bcftools call with a phased genotype caller upstream). Unphased input is rejected.
  3. Annotated GFF3 (annotated.gff3) — same GFF3 you passed to convert --to cds. Needed to map genome coordinates in the VCF onto CDS positions. Must be sort/pad/clean: the same file that produced the CDS, no later edits.
  4. Sample sheet (samples.tsv) — same schema as quant: sample_id, fastq_1, fastq_2 (or blank for SE), optional condition, batch, and arbitrary extra columns.
  5. Reference genome FASTA (genome.fa) — used as the decoy set in salmon's index.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
myconote-cli ase cds.fa \
    --vcf phased.vcf.gz \
    --gff3 annotated.gff3 \
    --samples samples.tsv \
    --genome genome.fa \
    -o ase_out

Then run the downstream binomial test with ase-template:

myconote-cli ase-template --ase-dir ase_out -o ase_analysis.R
Rscript ase_analysis.R

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: flag meaning <cds.fa> Reference CDS FASTA (positional, required). --vcf <phased.vcf[.gz]> Phased VCF. Unphased heterozygous sites cause a hard error with the offending line number. --gff3 <annotated.gff3> Same GFF3 that produced <cds.fa>. Required for genome → CDS coordinate mapping. --samples <sheet.tsv> Sample sheet (same schema as quant). --genome <genome.fa> Reference genome FASTA for decoy-aware indexing. --output <dir> / -o Output directory (default ase_out). --haplotype-names N1,N2 Custom haplotype labels (default hap0,hap1). Common alternative: paternal,maternal or Scer,Spar. -k <n> salmon k-mer length (default 31). --threads <n> / -t Threads per salmon / fastp run. --tmpdir <dir> Temp directory root for fastp-trimmed FASTQs (default $TMPDIR). --index-cache <dir> Index cache root (default $MYCONOTE_INDEX_CACHE or XDG). --keep-trimmed <dir> Persist fastp-trimmed FASTQs to this directory (off by default — deleted after quant). --max-indel-size <n> Skip indels longer than N bp, marked in variants_skipped.tsv (default 50). --asymmetry-threshold <f> Flag samples where |hap0 rate − hap1 rate| > f (default 0.05, i.e. 5 %). --seed <n> Deterministic seed (default 42). --fastp <path> Override fastp binary. --salmon <path> Override salmon binary.

docs.title: What gets skipped, and why
docs.text:
The VCF → personalized-CDS step is deliberately conservative — variants that could silently produce garbage are skipped and logged to variants_skipped.tsv with a reason:

  • unphased — heterozygous genotype without the | phase separator. Hard error, not a skip.
  • structural — non-SNV/MNP/indel variants (symbolic alleles, breakends).
  • multiallelic — sites with multiple ALT alleles; not represented in the current scheme.
  • missing_genotype — .|. or ./. at this site.
  • indel_too_large — indel length exceeds --max-indel-size (default 50 bp).
  • outside_cds — variant position doesn't fall inside any CDS exon.
  • spans_exon_boundary — indel spans an exon/intron boundary; introns aren't in the CDS.
  • ref_mismatch — VCF's REF allele doesn't match the genome FASTA at that position (VCF / genome version skew).
  • in_cis_overlap — multiple variants on the same haplotype overlap in CDS coordinates.

Counts for every category appear in ase_bundle.json under variants so downstream tools can summarize without re-deriving the list.

docs.title: Mapping-rate asymmetry
docs.text:
After both salmon runs finish, |mapping_rate_hap0 − mapping_rate_hap1| is computed for every sample. Anything over --asymmetry-threshold (default 5 %) emits a warning to stderr and sets asymmetry_flag = true in ase_bundle.json.

Strong asymmetry usually signals:

  • A phasing error — e.g. large haplotype blocks with the wrong parent-of-origin.
  • An assembly issue — one haplotype has many more accurate regions than the other.
  • A sample swap — the sample sheet claims one parent as hap0 when it's actually the other.

Not necessarily biology. Chase down the warning before interpreting the counts.

docs.title: Outputs (under <output-dir>)
docs.text: file contents cds_<hap>.fa One personalized CDS FASTA per haplotype (e.g. cds_hap0.fa, cds_hap1.fa). salmon/<sample>.<hap>/ One salmon output directory per sample × haplotype. Each contains the usual quant.sf, aux_info/, logs/. ase_counts.tsv Wide counts matrix: rows = transcripts, columns = <sample>.<hap>. ase_tpm.tsv Same shape as ase_counts.tsv, TPM-normalized. ase_summary.tsv Per-transcript metadata: informative flag, n_variants_hap0, n_variants_hap1, max_asymmetry. variants_applied.tsv Per-variant audit: which haplotype, which transcript, CDS position, strand. variants_skipped.tsv Per-variant audit: skip reason per category above. ase_bundle.json Reproducibility manifest (SHA256 of every input + tool versions + every skip count). fastp/<sample>.json Raw fastp JSON report per sample.

docs.title: What ase does NOT do
docs.text:
• Doesn't phase. Run a dedicated phaser (WhatsHap / HapCUT2) upstream. Unphased het sites are a hard error.
  • Doesn't variant-call. Bring your own VCF.
  • Doesn't do per-site ASE. This is transcript-level ASE (WASP / GATK ASEReadCounter operate at the site level — different problem shape).
  • Doesn't run the statistical test. See myconote-cli ase-template for the R script that does the binomial analysis on ase_counts.tsv.
  • Doesn't support >2 haplotypes in 0.5.0. Diploid-only for now; the code path is written to generalize to higher ploidy in 0.5.x.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Unphased heterozygous genotype at VCF line N" — your VCF has 0/1 where ASE needs 0|1. Run WhatsHap or HapCUT2 first, or use a caller that emits phased output (DeepVariant + read-backed phasing, GATK + VariantFiltration → WhatsHap phase).
  • "REF mismatch at chrX:12345" — VCF was called against a different genome build than --genome. Re-lift the VCF, or regenerate it against the same FASTA.
  • "spans_exon_boundary" count is very high — your indels fall on intron boundaries, which are outside the CDS. Not usually a bug; it's the reality of intronic variation in the VCF.
  • Low mapping rate on one haplotype — check the asymmetry warning in the bundle. If it's a phasing artifact, re-phase with longer reads or more stringent thresholds. If it's a real assembly gap, document it and proceed with the informative transcripts only.
  • "salmon: index not found" — --index-cache is not writable, or the cache slot got stale. Delete the cache directory or point to a fresh one.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• myconote-cli convert --to cds — prerequisite; produces cds.fa.
  • myconote-cli ase-template — emits the binomial-test R script for ase_counts.tsv.
  • myconote-cli quant — single-reference quantification (the non-ASE counterpart).
  • salmon documentation: https://salmon.readthedocs.io/
  • WhatsHap phaser: https://whatshap.readthedocs.io/

docs.title: myconote batch
docs.text:
Annotate multiple genomes in one command. Runs the full pipeline (sort, mask, predict, annotate, submit) per genome with progress tracking, resume support, and HTCondor integration.

myconote-cli batch <genomes_dir | sample_sheet.tsv> [options]

docs.title: Quick examples
docs.text:
# Annotate all FASTAs in a directory
myconote-cli batch genomes/ --kingdom fungi --threads 8

# Use a sample sheet for per-genome settings
myconote-cli batch samples.tsv --parallel 4

# Run only specific stages
myconote-cli batch genomes/ --stages sort,mask,predict

# Resume after interruption
myconote-cli batch --resume batch_out/

# Generate HTCondor submit files
myconote-cli batch genomes/ --condor --condor-mem 64G --condor-cpus 16

docs.title: Directory of FASTAs
docs.text:
Point batch at a directory containing .fa, .fasta, .fas, or .fna files:

myconote-cli batch genomes/

All genomes use the same settings (kingdom, genetic code, etc.) from CLI flags.

docs.title: Sample sheet (TSV)
docs.text:
For per-genome settings, provide a tab-separated file with a header row:

name        fasta                kingdom    species          genetic_code    locus_prefix
isolate_A   /data/isolate_A.fa   fungi      saccharomyces    1               ISOA
isolate_B   /data/isolate_B.fa   fungi      auto             12              ISOB
isolate_C   /data/isolate_C.fa   plant      arabidopsis      1               ISOC

Only the fasta column is required (also accepts path or genome as column names). All other columns are optional and use defaults when omitted.

Column Required Default Description name No FASTA filename stem Display name for this genome fasta Yes -- Path to input FASTA kingdom No fungi Kingdom for prediction species No auto Augustus species override genetic_code No 1 NCBI translation table locus_prefix No GENE Locus tag prefix

docs.title: Pipeline options
docs.text: Flag Default Description --output <dir> batch_out Batch output directory --stages <list> sort,mask,predict,annotate,submit Comma-separated stages to run --kingdom <k> fungi Default kingdom --threads <n> 4 Threads per genome --parallel <n> 2 Max genomes in parallel --min-length <bp> 500 Minimum contig length for sort --mask-engine <e> repeatmodeler Masking engine --genetic-code <n> 1 Default translation table --locus-prefix <s> GENE Default locus prefix --no-compare -- Skip auto-compare suggestion --resume <dir> -- Resume a previous batch run

docs.title: HTCondor options
docs.text: Flag Default Description --condor -- Generate HTCondor submit files (don't run locally) --condor-cpus <n> 8 CPUs per job --condor-mem <size> 32G Memory per job --condor-disk <size> 50G Disk per job --condor-queue <name> -- HTCondor accounting group --condor-extra <file> -- Extra submit directives to append

docs.text:
batch_out/
  status.json                    # batch state (for resume)
  isolate_A/
    isolate_A_sorted.fa
    isolate_A_masked.fa
    predict_out/
      consensus.gff3
    annotate_out/
      annotated.gff3
      proteins.fa
      annotations.tsv
    submit_out/
      annotation.tbl
  isolate_B/
    ...

docs.text: The dashboard auto-detects your environment:

docs.title: Interactive terminal (laptop, SSH session)
docs.text:
Live multi-progress bars showing per-genome stage progress:

  myconote batch -- 3 / 8 genomes complete

  v isolate_A    sort > mask > predict > annotate > submit   42m
  v isolate_B    sort > mask > predict > annotate > submit   38m
  * isolate_C    sort > mask > predict > update              27m
  * isolate_D    sort > mask > train                         14m
  . isolate_E    queued
  . isolate_F    queued

  [============---------------------------------------] 3/8 genomes (ETA ~2h15m)

docs.title: HPC batch job (no TTY)
docs.text:
Timestamped log lines, one per event:

[2026-04-16 14:30:22] isolate_A                      | sort       | started
[2026-04-16 14:31:05] isolate_A                      | sort       | done
[2026-04-16 14:31:05] isolate_A                      | mask       | started
...
[2026-04-16 16:45:33] isolate_E                      | predict    | FAILED -- Augustus exit code 1
...
[2026-04-16 18:12:01] isolate_A                      | ALL        | done (3720s)

Monitor with tail -f slurm-12345.out or condor_tail -f job_0.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
A status.json file is written after every stage completion. If the process is interrupted:

myconote-cli batch --resume batch_out/

This reads the state file, skips completed stages, and picks up where it left off. Per-genome, per-stage granularity -- if genome A completed sort+mask but failed on predict, resume reruns predict for genome A and continues with the remaining genomes.

docs.title: HTCondor integration
docs.text:
Generate submit files instead of running locally:

myconote-cli batch genomes/ --condor --condor-mem 64G --condor-cpus 16

This creates:

File Description condor.sub HTCondor submit file run_genome.sh Wrapper script executed by each job condor_genomes.txt Per-genome argument list (tab-separated) condor_logs/ Directory for per-job log/output/error files

Submit to the cluster:

condor_submit batch_out/condor.sub

Monitor:

condor_q                                      # job status
tail -f batch_out/condor_logs/job_0.out       # first job output
condor_tail -f <cluster_id>.0                 # live output

Each genome runs as a separate job. The wrapper script chains the pipeline stages sequentially within each job. Jobs use the shared filesystem -- no file transfer needed.

docs.title: Custom HTCondor directives
docs.text:
Append extra submit directives from a file:

myconote-cli batch genomes/ --condor --condor-extra extra.sub

Example extra.sub:

+WantGPU = true
requirements = (OpSysAndVer == "Ubuntu22")
notification = Complete
notify_user = you@wisc.edu

docs.title: Auto-compare
docs.text:
When 2 or more genomes complete successfully, batch prints a suggested compare command:

  Next: myconote-cli compare batch_out/**/annotate_out/*.gff3

Disable with --no-compare.
