docs.title: A/B: Augustus self-training and protein-hints lift (v0.7.11)
docs.text: Reproducibility + methods record for the corrected A/B that tests whether two MycoNote accuracy levers — Augustus self-training and miniprot protein hints — actually raise gene-prediction F1 once two provisioning/filter defects are fixed. Written against commit 5ea962a (v0.7.11).

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
Earlier A/B rounds (v0.7.9–v0.7.10) showed neither lever lifting loose/strict gene-level F1. Diagnosis found the levers never got a fair test:

  1. Self-training never ran. Augustus new_species.pl aborted with Could not open .../augustus_config//species/generic/generic_parameters.cfg and MycoNote silently fell back to a stock species. Root cause: MycoNote's setup --dbs augustus-fungi fetched only the curated per-species dirs from the Augustus GitHub mirror and omitted species/generic/, the template new_species.pl copies to seed a new species.
  2. Protein hints fed whole-kingdom OrthoDB with no identity filter. The A/B fed ~/.myconote/dbs/orthodb/Fungi.fa (all-fungi, ~3.9 GB) straight to the DIAMOND prefilter with only an e-value cutoff. On the one completed replicate (cne) loose was flat and strict dropped (0.526 → 0.49).

This A/B asks: with species/generic/ provisioned and with a percent-identity gate on the protein prefilter, do the levers lift?

docs.title: Literature basis for the fixes
docs.text:
• Self-training / config: the community fix for the missing-generic / non-writable AUGUSTUS_CONFIG_PATH error is to copy the whole Augustus config/ tree (generic included) to a writable location (BRAKER issue #23; funannotate issue #118, PR #1222 find_augustus_base; TAMU HPRC guide). funannotate rsyncs the entire config, so it never hits the missing-generic bug. v0.7.11 provisions species/generic/ the same way, within MycoNote's curated-download model.
  • Protein hints / identity gate: GALBA (Brůna et al., miniprot + Augustus) recommends proteins of the closest relatives, not broad remote databases, and warns miniprot "may produce spurious alignments if the reference proteins originate from distantly related species," adding a miniprothint scorer to filter them. BRAKER3 (Gabriel et al.) reports higher F1 with a species-excluded close-relative DB than with a large remote one. funannotate's default protein evidence is UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot (curated/compact), mapped by exonerate at a default 80 % identity. v0.7.11's --protein-hints-min-identity is MycoNote's equivalent identity gate on the DIAMOND prefilter.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Genomes (6-genome benchmark subset used here): ani (A. nidulans), ncr (N. crassa), cne (C. neoformans JEC21). Masked FASTA, Augustus species, genetic code and the seqid rename-table are reused verbatim from each genome's baseline rep1 (results/myconote/<id>/rep1/) so only the one tested flag varies vs baseline.
  • Reference annotations: data/<id>/reference.gff3.
  • Protein DB (protein-hints arms): ~/.myconote/dbs/orthodb/Fungi.fa (OrthoDB fungal partition) — deliberately the same DB as the no-gate baseline arm, so the identity gate is the only changed variable.
  • species/generic/ template: 8 generic_* files copied into ~/.myconote/augustus_config/species/ (stopgap identical to what the fixed setup --dbs augustus-fungi now produces).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Harness: ~/ab_v077/run_ab.sh <genome_id> <feature> <benchmark_dir> (non-repo), one Condor job per (feature × genome). Per job:

myconote-cli predict <masked.fa> --kingdom fungi --species <SP> \
    --locus-prefix <ID> --output <out>/predict --threads 8 <FLAG>
myconote-cli annotate <out>/predict/consensus.gff3 --fasta <masked.fa> \
    --output <out>/annotate --kingdom fungi --locus-prefix <ID> \
    --genetic-code <code> --threads 8
python3 scripts/compare_annotations.py <out>/annotate/annotated.gff3 \
    <reference.gff3> --rename-table <rename_table.tsv> --output <out>/metrics.json

<FLAG> per arm:

arm FLAG baseline (none — stock species / ab-initio, from each genome's rep1) selftrain --augustus-training self prothints --protein-hints Fungi.fa (no-gate control) prothints70 --protein-hints Fungi.fa --protein-hints-min-identity 70

Submits: condor_submit ab_selftrain.sub (ncr, cne), ab_prothints70.sub (ani, ncr, cne). Baseline protein-hints (no-gate) is clusters 145951 (ani, ncr, cne). Build: cluster 145978 (v0.7.11, myco_build conda env, cargo install --locked --offline), then ~/.cargo/bin synced to ~/.local/bin (run scripts prepend ~/.local/bin; a stale copy there has shadowed rebuilds before).

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: compare_annotations.py — Eilbeck et al. (2009) gene/exon/nucleotide F1. Strict gene match = identical ordered CDS structure (CDS-to-CDS); loose = locus overlap. Metric reported: gene_level.{loose,strict}.F1.

docs.title: Tool / software versions
docs.text: • MycoNote-CLI v0.7.11 (5ea962a); Augustus 3.3.3 (not AVX2 — runs full node pool); SNAP; GeneMark-ES/EP (gmes_linux_64_4); DIAMOND (prefilter); miniprot (protein-to-genome); Python 3 (scorer). Built with the myco_build conda env.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Per arm: results/ab/<feature>/<genome>/{predict,annotate,metrics.json,*.log}.
  • Engagement evidence lives in predict.log: self-train prints Trained species: … on success or the loud SELF-TRAINING DID NOT RUN banner on fallback (now naming which gate failed); the gated prefilter logs evalue ≤ …, identity ≥ 70% and the kept-protein count.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Verdict: neither lever lifts gene-level F1. Both fixes corrected the mechanics they targeted, and the accuracy did not move. The accuracy chase through these two levers was closed on 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Self-training (clusters 146281; generic/ provisioned)
docs.text:
The species/generic/ fix cleared the second blocker: new_species.pl now succeeds and creates the trained species dir (ncr_trained, cne_trained, each with *_parameters.cfg etc. on disk). But a third blocker surfaced — etraining then fails on MycoNote's first-pass training-gene input:

Running etraining…
!! WARNING: Augustus SELF-TRAINING DID NOT RUN !!
reason: Invalid GFF format: etraining failed. Check train_out/etraining.log
using species: neurospora_crassa (stock / pre-trained fallback)

The SNAP self-training path failed on the same run (fathom … -categorize 1000 failed). Root cause (found 2026-10-11, fixed in v0.7.12, a2b09aa): MycoNote's native GenBank writer omitted the source 1..<len> feature that Augustus etraining uses to set each record's sequence bounds. Without it, every CDS was rejected as "out of range. Ignoring it." (6963/8703 on ncr), the training set emptied, etraining exited non-zero, and prediction fell back to the stock species — giving the byte-identical pre-fix numbers (ncr 0.8971/0.5638, cne 0.9217/0.5267). Verified: canonical gff2gbSmallDNA.pl records (which carry source) etrain with 0 out-of-range; injecting source into MycoNote's own records drops out-of-range 6963→0 and etraining completes.

With the fix (v0.7.12), self-training runs end to end but underperforms the stock species. etraining completes (0 out-of-range), ncr_trained / cne_trained are built and used:

genome stock baseline loose/strict self-trained loose/strict n genes ncr 0.897 / 0.564 0.796 / 0.525 7336 cne 0.921 / 0.526 0.788 / 0.515 4642 (stock ~7253)

Self-training lowers F1 by 0.10–0.13 (loose) here. Expected: the training set is MycoNote's own first-pass ab-initio calls (errors propagate), there is no optimize_augustus.pl meta-parameter pass, and these benchmark fungi already have excellent hand-curated stock Augustus models. For a novel fungus with no close stock species the trade could differ, but on well-represented model fungi stock wins. This reinforces the accuracy-thread closure: the lever now works and still does not help. A residual non-fatal etraining warning (stopCodonExcludedFromCDS; MycoNote's CDS excludes the stop codon) is a model- tuning item, not a training blocker.

docs.title: Protein hints (clusters 145951 no-gate, 146282 gate70)
docs.text:
The identity gate works exactly as designed and still changes nothing. On cne the 70 % gate dropped the prefiltered set from 312 → 207 proteins (105 distant homologs removed), and F1 was unchanged and strictly below the ab-initio baseline either way:

genome baseline loose/strict no-gate (n prot) loose/strict gate70 (n prot) loose/strict cne 0.921 / 0.526 (312) 0.9244 / 0.490 (207) 0.9243 / 0.491 ani 0.897 / 0.445 (rep still draining) (179) 0.9041 / 0.432 ncr 0.897 / 0.564 (rep still draining) (rep still draining)

Pattern confirmed on both completed genomes (cne, ani gate70): vs ab-initio baseline, protein hints leave loose ~flat (cne −0.000, ani +0.007) and nudge strict down (cne 0.526→0.491, ani 0.445→0.432). Mechanism: MycoNote's agreement-weighted consensus is dominated by the ab-initio predictors (Augustus / SNAP / GeneMark); miniprot protein evidence — whether 312, 207, or 179 proteins — does not shift the merge and slightly lowers strict. Not a provisioning artifact: the lever functions correctly and does not help this architecture. The remaining no-gate ani/ncr and gate70 ncr reps were still draining when the decision was taken; they do not bear on the conclusion and are left to land on disk at results/ab/prothints{,70}/<g>/metrics.json.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Stop pursuing prediction accuracy through self-training and protein hints. Lock MycoNote's positioning on its demonstrated strengths (fast ab-initio prediction, complete functional annotation, x86-64-v2 portability vs the AVX2-compiled Augustus in funannotate/BRAKER). The v0.7.11 code (generic provisioning, loud-failing self-train preflight, opt-in --protein-hints-min-identity) stays: each is correct on its own merit even though neither raised F1.

docs.title: Key decisions / caveats
docs.text:
• The protein-hints gate is tested on the same all-fungi OrthoDB as the no-gate control, so the comparison isolates the identity filter. It does NOT test the orthogonal lever the literature also favours — swapping the DB for a Swiss-Prot / close-relative set. If the 70 % gate alone does not lift, a DB swap is the next test, not another gate tweak.
  • --protein-hints-min-identity default is 0 (off): v0.7.11 does not silently change existing behaviour; the gate is opt-in and the A/B picks the operating point.
  • Self-training provisioning used a cp stopgap of species/generic/ from the myconote_augustus conda env; functionally identical to the fixed setup path, chosen only to avoid a re-download before the A/B.

docs.title: Benchmark plan — MycoNote-CLI vs funannotate / MAKER / BRAKER (publication-grade)
docs.text: Governing design document and Methods raw material for the definitive four-tool fungal-annotation benchmark. Synthesises the harness-engineering and statistical-design reviews (2026-10-13). Execution is phased with the steps in §7.

docs.title: 1. Replication unit (the central design decision)
docs.text: The independent replication unit is the genome, not the per-tool jobs. - Accuracy is near-deterministic (within-genome rep SD ≤ 0.001 F1). The 3 reps are a determinism audit only — collapse to the per-genome mean and analyse at the genome level. Treating 18 jobs as n=18 is pseudoreplication. - Timing reps carry real HPC-noise variance — keep them, analyse on per-genome medians / log-ratios; reps are nested within genome.

docs.title: 2. Genome panel (expanded + balanced + scaling)
docs.text:
Target ~13–16 genomes, ≥4 per subphylum, ≥3 Basidiomycota, +1 Taphrinomycotina outgroup, +scaling tests. Curated references required for all.

clade genomes (accession) Saccharomycotina sce, cal, ylp (existing) + K. lactis GCF_000002515.2, K. phaffii GCF_001708105.1 Pezizomycotina ani, ncr (existing) + F. graminearum GCF_000240135.3, A. fumigatus GCF_000002655.1 Basidiomycota cne (existing) + U. maydis GCF_000328475.2, C. cinerea GCF_000182895.1 Taphrinomycotina S. pombe GCF_000002945.2 (PomBase, gold-standard outgroup) scaling Tuber melanosporum GCF_000151645.1 (~125 Mb, repeat-rich) or Z. tritici GCF_000219625.1 (~40 Mb); + one controlled fragmentation test (shred an existing genome to draft N50, same reference)

docs.title: 3. Measurement
docs.text:
• Enforce AVX2 requirements = (TARGET.has_avx2 =?= true) on ALL 4 .sub files (committed) + same-node pinning for the timing production run.
  • BRAKER timing: wrap braker.pl in /usr/bin/time -v (its own performance.json is all-zeros); log-span fallback only if wrapping fails.
  • RSS: report per-stage (predict vs annotate) peak RSS on a log-axis figure.
  • Per-source annotate timing: instrument annotate to emit per-source wall-time (swissprot/pfam/busco/cazyme/merops/eggnog) — the Pfam-dominates finding needs error bars.
  • Pinned-node wall-time is the headline; CPU-seconds is the robustness check.

docs.title: 4. Statistics (randomized complete block; genome = block)
docs.text:
• Per metric (loose/strict/nt F1): Friedman omnibus + Nemenyi post-hoc (exploratory); exact Wilcoxon signed-rank for the pre-registered MycoNote-vs-funannotate primary contrast.
  • Effect sizes: rank-biserial, Cliff's δ, exact 64-permutation CI; Kendall's W.
  • Timing: LMM log(time) ~ tool + (1|genome) + (tool|genome) (Kenward–Roger), with median-based Friedman as the outlier-robust primary. Fair arms only.
  • Multiplicity: Holm for the confirmatory family (myco-vs-fun × 3 accuracy + 2 speed); BH-FDR for the exploratory 4-tool grid; per-metric separate; report corrected + uncorrected.
  • Clade = descriptive stratum, not a tested factor (Basidiomycota n=1 → tool×clade non-estimable). Report the pattern descriptively.
  • Equivalence claims need TOST (margin ±0.02 F1), not NHST non-significance.
  • Power: n=6 detects only ΔF1 ≳ 0.05 consistent; ~10–15 for ΔF1 ≈ 0.05; ~25–50 for ΔF1 ≈ 0.02–0.03 → the panel expansion (§2) is the power lever.

docs.title: 5. Deeper risks to pre-empt
docs.text:

docs.title: What this documents and why
docs.text: The BRAKER3 arm of the 4-tool gene-annotation benchmark (MycoNote vs MAKER vs funannotate vs BRAKER) failed on the GLBRC HTCondor pool: a full 18-job run (cluster 145888) produced braker.gtf for only the jobs that happened to land on AVX2-capable execute nodes. This README records the root cause and the fix so the result is reproducible and the Methods section is accurate.

docs.title: Root cause (diagnosed from cluster 145888 logs)
docs.text:
augustus 3.5.0 in the myconote_braker3 conda env is compiled with AVX2 (1912 ymm instruction references; 0 zmm/AVX-512 — confirmed via objdump -d .../bin/augustus | grep -c '%ymm'). On execute nodes WITHOUT AVX2 (microarch x86_64-v2, e.g. scarcity-10) augustus aborts with SIGILL — "Illegal instruction (core dumped)" — at braker.pl line 2551 (the config-time augustus self-test). braker.pl then reports "augustus not executable on this machine" and exits 1 with no braker.gtf.

condor_history 145888 showed procs 3–17 (15 jobs) were all matched to scarcity-10 and all exited 1; the jobs that landed on AVX2 nodes (scarcity-20 = x86_64-v4, scarcity-3 = x86_64-v3) either scored (sce rep2) or ran the full pipeline fine (GeneMark-EP completed, Augustus training proceeded). So the failure is purely a CPU-instruction-set vs node-placement mismatch; it is NOT a GeneMark-EP failure (GeneMark-EP succeeds on AVX2 nodes). The earlier LD_LIBRARY_PATH fix addressed a different, missing-shared-lib case and does not help a SIGILL.

Node CPU features (from condor_status -af Machine Microarch has_avx2): scarcity-10 x86_64-v2 has_avx2 = false -> augustus SIGILL (all jobs failed) scarcity-3 x86_64-v3 has_avx2 = true -> augustus OK, full pipeline runs scarcity-20 x86_64-v4 has_avx2 = true -> augustus OK, sce rep2 scored

docs.title: The fix
docs.text:
1. jobs/braker.sub: add requirements = (TARGET.has_avx2 =?= true) so HTCondor only matches BRAKER jobs to AVX2-capable execute nodes (188 slots / 15 machines available at fix time). The =?= operator treats an undefined ad as false, so nodes that do not publish the feature are safely excluded.
  2. jobs/run_braker.sh: add a loud AVX2 preflight (grep -qw avx2 /proc/cpuinfo) that exits early with an actionable message if a job is ever mis-scheduled to a non-AVX2 node — so the failure is legible instead of a buried SIGILL.

Neither change alters the annotation algorithm or BRAKER parameters, so the tool comparison stays fair. The only change is WHERE jobs are allowed to run.

docs.title: CAZyme annotation fix — dbCAN HMMER path (benchmark myconote arm)
docs.text: Status: RESOLVED (v0.7.15). CAZyme annotation in the MycoNote benchmark arm now runs an hmmsearch of the predicted proteins against the dbCAN HMM database, the same method the funannotate arm uses, so the two pipelines are directly comparable. Verified on S. cerevisiae (see Verification below).

docs.title: Why this exists (the question it answers)
docs.text: The functional-annotation comparison claims MycoNote and funannotate both annotate CAZymes (carbohydrate-active enzymes). A pre-submission check found the MycoNote arm was emitting no CAZyme calls — annotate --cazyme was silently doing nothing — which would have made the CAZyme comparison an unfair asymmetry (funannotate reports CAZymes; MycoNote reported none).

docs.title: Root causes (all verified with real commands on the cluster)
docs.text:
1. Corrupt dbCAN database. ~/.myconote/dbs/dbcan/CAZyDB.fa and dbCAN-HMMdb-V12.txt were both 18,618-byte HTML error pages (head → <!DOCTYPE html; grep -c "^>" = 0) saved by a failed 2025-07-09 download.
  2. No reachable CAZyme backend. run_myconote.sh passed --cazyme with no database flag. MycoNote's cazyme::dbcan_available() probes which run_dbcan.py; the installed dbCAN entrypoint is run_dbcan (v3.0.7, no .py), so the probe failed and annotate hit the "No dbCAN backend" branch.
  3. dbCAN2 → dbCAN3 incompatibility. Even exposed, dbCAN 3.0.7's overview.txt columns (Gene ID | EC# | HMMER | dbCAN_sub | DIAMOND) differ from the dbCAN2 layout (Gene ID | HMMER | Hotpep | DIAMOND) MycoNote's parser read, so driving run_dbcan 3.0.7 unchanged would have misparsed families.

An interim DIAMOND fallback (blastp vs the full CAZyDB sequence set) was tried and rejected: it over-called CAZymes ~16× — 2,174 of 5,773 S. cerevisiae genes (37.7 %) — because sequence similarity to a full-length multidomain CAZy protein is not family-domain membership. DIAMOND-blastp is not a valid CAZyme comparator here.

docs.title: The fix (v0.7.15)
docs.text:
A native HMMER path in src/annotate/cazyme.rs:

  • run_hmmer_cazyme() runs hmmsearch --domtblout of the proteins against the dbCAN HMM database, reusing the same engine/approach as the Pfam step.
  • parse_dbcan_domtblout() applies the canonical dbCAN cutoffs — HMM-profile coverage > 0.35, and domain i-E-value < 1e-15 (tightened to < 1e-18 when the aligned HMM span ≤ 80 aa) — and keeps the best (lowest-E) hit per (gene, family). Family = HMM name with a trailing .hmm stripped (GH5.hmm → GH5).
  • New flag --cazyme-hmm <dbCAN.hmm>. Backend precedence: --cazyme-hmm (hmmsearch) → run_dbcan → --cazyme-db (DIAMOND fallback).

This is funannotate's method: both arms hmmsearch the proteins against the dbCAN HMM profiles.

  • dbCAN HMM database (primary): ~/.myconote/dbs/funannotate/dbCAN.hmm (100,916,453 bytes) + pressed indices .h3{f,i,m,p}; dbCAN HMMdb 14.0, CAZyDB 2025-07-10 (provisioned earlier by funannotate setup -d). This is the identical HMM database funannotate's arm uses.

Re-ran annotate on the existing S. cerevisiae predict output (5,773 predicted genes):

metric DIAMOND fallback (rejected) HMMER (shipped) CAZyme annotations (rows) 2,174 333 distinct genes called 2,174 (37.7 %) 136 (2.36 %) rows with junk family label 992 (46 %) 0 distinct families 830 (inflated) 104 cazyme step wall time ~44 s ~41 s

  • dbCAN HMMdb version (14.0, CAZyDB 2025-07-10) matches the funannotate arm exactly by design — both consume the same dbCAN.hmm.

docs.title: Fairness: timing-node pinning decision (FLAGGED)
docs.text:
§3 calls for same-node pinning of the 4 tools per genome. On this shared pool strict same-node pinning (Machine == "<one host>") is infeasible: - Only 15 AVX2 hosts exist, heterogeneous (6–102 cores); the pool carries 500–700 idle jobs from other users. - Pinning a genome's whole tool×rep block to one named host serialises ~20–40 jobs onto a single contended machine and stalls BRAKER (16c/64 GB) indefinitely.

Closest fair alternative adopted (exactly the §-anticipated fallback, "pin to one node class + report CPU-time"): pin all four arms to one microarch generation, x86_64-v3, so wall-time is compared on identical-ISA hardware. - The AVX2 pool splits into x86_64-v3 (9 hosts: scarcity-1,2,3,4,11,12,14,18,19) and x86_64-v4 (6 hosts). v3 chosen: more hosts (throughput, less contention) and more large-memory hosts able to seat BRAKER's 16c/64 GB slot (scarcity-11/12/18/19). - Requirement on every timing sub: requirements = (TARGET.has_avx2 =?= true) && (TARGET.Microarch =?= "x86_64-v3") (matchmaking verified satisfiable: 27 slots match). - CPU-seconds (performance.json total_cpu_seconds, captured by every wrapper via /usr/bin/time -v) is reported alongside wall-time as the co-tenant-contention-robust check. True single-tenant isolation is impossible on a partitionable-slot shared pool regardless of pinning, which is the independent reason CPU-seconds is reported. - Accuracy runs are NOT pinned (deterministic, hardware-independent).

  • scaling.tsv (56) — genome, size_mb, clade, tool, wall_min_median.
  • gene_counts.tsv (56) — genome, tool, n_pred_genes_mean, n_ref_genes.
  • clade_strata.tsv (56) — same columns as accuracy.tsv (clade-stratified view).

  • completeness.tsv (28) — BUSCO-of-predicted-proteins, MycoNote + funannotate ONLY (MAKER/BRAKER dirs carry no protein-BUSCO). CAVEAT: different lineages/BUSCO versions (myconote fungi_odb10 n=758 BUSCO v5; funannotate dikarya_odb9 n=1312 BUSCO v3) → NOT a fair cross-tool axis; no figure drawn from it.

docs.title: Preliminary MycoNote vs funannotate comparison (1-rep smoke)
docs.text:
⚠ Numbers below predate the scorer fix (2026-10-15). The gene/exon F1 values in the table and figure were produced before compare_annotations.py was fixed to count protein-coding reference genes only (commit 99cbefc). That fix changes every genome's gene/exon F1 (nucleotide F1 is unchanged), and corrects the spom artifact noted below: spom gene-loose F1 goes 0.58 → 0.93 (ref genes 12,613 → 5,124) for MycoNote, and funannotate's spom corrects the same way. The production run uses the fixed scorer; treat the figure/table here as the pre-fix snapshot.

Status: PRELIMINARY. This is a 1-replicate comparison built from the expanded-panel smoke runs while the MAKER/BRAKER smokes finish. The production matrix (n=10 timing reps, 3 accuracy reps, all four tools, proper statistics) supersedes these numbers — do not cite these as final.

docs.title: What this does / why
docs.text: Side-by-side MycoNote (v0.7.15) vs funannotate (v1.8.17) on the 14-genome fungal panel: gene / exon / nucleotide accuracy vs the RefSeq reference, plus wall-clock time. Gives an early read on where MycoNote stands before the full run.

docs.title: Inputs / provenance (pinned)
docs.text:
• MycoNote v0.7.15 — results_smoke_expanded_v0715/myconote/<id>/rep1 (all 14 genomes, fresh this session; HMMER CAZyme path).
  • funannotate v1.8.17:
  • 8 new genomes (klac, kpha, fgra, afum, umay, ccin, spom, tmel) — fresh this session, results_smoke_expanded_competitors/funannotate/<id>/rep1.
  • 6 original genomes (sce, cal, ylp, ani, ncr, cne) — prior fair-run rep1 from results/funannotate/<id>/rep1 (same v1.8.17, same references, same compare_annotations.py). CAVEAT: different run session/node than the 8 new ones, so cross-genome timing carries that provenance difference; accuracy is version-/reference-matched and comparable.
  • Accuracy metric: scripts/compare_annotations.py (Eilbeck-style gene/exon/ nucleotide TP/FP/FN → F1), identical for both tools, against the same data/<id>/reference.gff3.
  • Timing: each run's performance.json (/usr/bin/time -v per stage; AVX2- pinned nodes both arms).

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
# pull the per-run JSONs, collate, and render the figure
python3 compare_myco_fun.py          # (uses ~/miniconda3 python with matplotlib)

compare_myco_fun.py reads the pulled metrics.json + performance.json for both tools and writes comparison_myconote_vs_funannotate.tsv and figure_myconote_vs_funannotate.{pdf,png}.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• comparison_myconote_vs_funannotate.tsv — per-genome, per-tool: predicted gene count, gene F1 (loose/strict), exon F1 (exact), nucleotide F1, predict / annotate / total wall-minutes, peak RSS (GB).
  • figure_myconote_vs_funannotate.{pdf,png} — 4 panels: (a) gene F1 loose, (b) gene F1 strict, (c) nucleotide F1, (d) total wall-clock. MycoNote (blue) vs funannotate (orange), Okabe-Ito; * marks the 8 new genomes.

docs.title: Results (win tally across 14 genomes)
docs.text:
metric better MycoNote funannotate tie gene F1 (loose) higher 1 13 0 gene F1 (strict) higher 6 8 0 exon F1 (exact) higher 5 9 0 nucleotide F1 higher 10 4 0 total wall-clock lower 10 4 0

Read: funannotate has a small, consistent edge on gene-level detection (loose F1, margins ~0.01–0.04); the two are roughly even on exact CDS structure (strict); MycoNote leads on nucleotide-level accuracy and is faster overall on most genomes.

docs.title: Caveats / things to run down before production
docs.text:
• Proxy Augustus models underperform (expected). MycoNote's two genomes with no species-exact Augustus model — kpha (pichia_stipitis) and tmel (aspergillus_nidulans) — are its weakest: kpha strict F1 0.568 vs 0.758, tmel nucleotide F1 0.561 vs 0.664. This is the flagged nearest-clade-proxy penalty, not a general accuracy gap. funannotate trains Augustus per-genome via --busco_seed_species, which sidesteps it (a design difference the benchmark characterizes).
  • spom likely a scoring artifact. Both tools score gene-loose F1 ~0.58 while nucleotide F1 is ~0.98. High nucleotide + low gene-level for both tools points to a spom reference/gene-ID matching issue in compare_annotations.py, not a real failure — investigate before the production run.
  • tmel is hard for both (repeat-rich 125 Mb truffle); low F1 across the board.
  • 1 replicate only. No variance, no significance testing. The production matrix adds reps and the Friedman/Wilcoxon/LMM statistics from BENCHMARK_PLAN.md.

docs.title: myconote-cli annotate
docs.text:
myconote-cli annotate --help

See the Pipeline Overview for how annotate fits into the full workflow.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
annotate takes the gene GFF3 as a positional argument and the genome via --fasta:

myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 \
    --fasta genome_masked.fa \
    --genetic-code 1 \
    --threads 8 \
    --output annotate_out/

Output is written as annotated.gff3 (plus per-source tables and a BUSCO summary) in the output directory.

docs.title: Functional sources
docs.text:
The core sources run by default: MMseqs2 (Swiss-Prot homology), Pfam domains (--no-pfam to skip), and BUSCO completeness (--no-busco to skip). The rest are opt-in — add the flag to enable each:

Source Flag Database Provides MMseqs2 default on Swiss-Prot Gene names, best-hit species Pfam default on (--no-pfam) Pfam-A (hmmsearch) Protein domain families BUSCO default on (--no-busco) fungi_odb10 Completeness assessment EggNOG --eggnog EggNOG / COG GO terms, KEGG, COG categories CAZyme --cazyme dbCAN (DIAMOND) Carbohydrate-active enzymes MEROPS --merops MEROPS (DIAMOND) Protease families antiSMASH --antismash antiSMASH Secondary-metabolite clusters InterProScan --interproscan EBI REST Domain + GO cross-refs secretome --secretome DeepSig + DeepTMHMM Secreted-protein prediction tRNAscan-SE --trnascan — tRNA gene prediction 
# Core (default): MMseqs2 + Pfam + BUSCO
myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 --fasta genome_masked.fa --output annotate_out/

# Full: add the opt-in sources
myconote-cli annotate predict_out/consensus.gff3 --fasta genome_masked.fa \
    --eggnog --cazyme --merops --antismash --secretome --trnascan --interproscan \
    --threads 8 --output annotate_out/

docs.title: EggNOG speed (v0.7.8)
docs.text: The EggNOG step runs ~4× faster by default: emapper.py is called with --dmnd_iterate no (measured ~46 min vs ~3.4 h on a 10,655-protein proteome, at identical recall). To restore the slower, maximum-recall DIAMOND iterate path, pass --eggnog-iterate.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
MycoNote-CLI organises genome annotation into seven sequential commands. Each command produces standard-format output files that feed directly into the next step.

┌──────┐  ┌──────┐  ┌───────┐  ┌─────────┐  ┌────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌────────┐
│ sort │→ │ mask │→ │ train │→ │ predict │→ │ update │→ │ annotate │→ │ submit │
└──────┘  └──────┘  └───────┘  └─────────┘  └────────┘  └──────────┘  └────────┘
Step Command What it does Key tools 1 sort Reorder + length-filter contigs (lossless by default; --ncbi-clean to rename) Built-in 2 mask Identify and soft-mask repetitive elements RepeatModeler2, RepeatMasker 3 train Train gene predictors on RNA evidence PASA, Trinity, Augustus training 4 predict Predict gene models ab initio + consensus Augustus, GlimmerHMM, SNAP, GeneMark, miniprot 5 update Refine models with RNA-seq PASA update 6 annotate Assign functional annotations MMseqs2, eggNOG, dbCAN, InterProScan 7 submit Prepare NCBI GenBank submission table2asn, built-in validation

You can start the pipeline at any step if you already have intermediate files. For example, if you have a masked genome and trained Augustus parameters, you can jump straight to predict.

docs.title: Multi-genome mode
docs.text:
For projects with multiple genomes, use batch to run the full pipeline across all of them:

myconote-cli batch genomes/ --kingdom fungi --threads 8
myconote-cli batch samples.tsv --condor   # HTCondor HPC submission

See batch documentation for details on sample sheets, HTCondor, and resume.

docs.title: AI-powered interpretation
docs.text:
After any stage, use explain to interpret the results:

myconote-cli explain predict              # full: rules + local LLM
myconote-cli explain predict --no-llm     # rules only

See explain documentation for details.

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text:
Pipeline commands take the input as a positional argument (not a --genome flag) and write to a path given by --output/-o. Common flags:

Flag Description <input> (positional) Input genome FASTA / GFF3 for that stage --output, -o Output path (file or directory, per command) --threads CPU threads where the stage uses them (e.g. predict, annotate; sort has none) --kingdom fungi (default, primary use case). plant / animal / insect / protist accepted but experimental — see the multi-kingdom note on the home page. --species / --clade Override the Augustus species model (predict); --clade picks a clade-appropriate fungal default

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Description NCBI_EMAIL Used by BLAST remote queries AUGUSTUS_CONFIG_PATH Override Augustus config directory MYCONOTE_CHAT_ENDPOINT Override Ollama endpoint for explain MYCONOTE_CHAT_MODEL Override LLM model for explain MYCONOTE_CHAT_API_KEY Optional API key for LLM endpoint

docs.title: myconote-cli predict
docs.text:
myconote-cli predict --help

See the Pipeline Overview for how predict fits into the full workflow.

docs.title: Choosing the Augustus species model (--clade)
docs.text:
Augustus needs a species model. By default a fungal run uses saccharomyces_cerevisiae_S288C, but that is a Saccharomycotina model and a poor choice off that clade — so instead of hard-coding it, pass --clade to get a clade-appropriate default:

myconote-cli predict genome_masked.fa --kingdom fungi --clade pezizomycotina
--clade Default model saccharomycotina saccharomyces_cerevisiae_S288C pezizomycotina aspergillus_nidulans basidiomycota cryptococcus_neoformans_neoformans_JEC21

An explicit --species <model> always wins. A fungal run with neither --species nor --clade still uses S288C but prints a warning (BUSCO completeness can fall below 15 % off-Saccharomycotina).

docs.title: Protein hints (--protein-hints)
docs.text:
Add protein evidence from related species as Augustus hints via miniprot. The protein DB is prefiltered with diamond blastx so a whole-kingdom OrthoDB set does not stall miniprot:

myconote-cli predict genome_masked.fa --kingdom fungi --species aspergillus_nidulans \
    --protein-hints orthodb_fungi.fa --protein-hints-min-identity 70
Flag Default Description --protein-hints <proteins.fa> off Protein FASTA → miniprot → Augustus hints --protein-hints-evalue <E> 1e-5 diamond e-value for the prefilter --protein-hints-max <N> 50000 Max proteins fed to miniprot (0 = unbounded) --protein-hints-min-identity <P> 0 Keep only prefilter hits ≥ P% identity — raise it to drop distant, low-identity homologs (close relatives beat remote proteins)

This path is non-fatal: if diamond/miniprot are absent or nothing survives the prefilter, prediction proceeds ab-initio. (Distinct from --protein-fasta, which feeds GeneMark EP+/ETP+ via ProtHint — see below.)

docs.title: Self-training Augustus (--augustus-training self)
docs.text: --augustus-training stock (default) uses a curated pre-trained species. --augustus-training self instead trains a genome-specific model on the fly (first-pass prediction → new_species.pl → etraining). It needs the Augustus companion scripts and the species/generic/ template from setup --db augustus-fungi; if either is missing, predict prints a loud banner and falls back to the stock species (it never silently pretends to train). On fungi with a curated model, stock usually wins — self-train earns its keep on a novel fungus with no close stock species.

docs.title: Choosing a GeneMark mode
docs.text:
gmes_petap.pl ships four self-training algorithms. Pick one with --genemark-mode <mode>; if you don't pass the flag, GeneMark is skipped.

Mode Flag Extra inputs required Quality When to use ES --genemark-mode es none Lowest No RNA-seq, no protein database. Fast smoke run. ET --genemark-mode et --genemark-hints <introns.gff> Medium RNA-seq available; HISAT2 / STAR splice-junctions converted to GFF. EP+ --genemark-mode ep --protein-fasta <proteins.fa> High No RNA-seq but a curated protein DB exists. Recommended for novel CTG-clade fungi — the alt-yeast nuclear code makes published predictors unreliable, and protein evidence anchors the training. ETP+ --genemark-mode etp both --genemark-hints and --protein-fasta Highest Both data types in hand. Same accuracy ceiling as BRAKER3 but driven by GeneMark alone.

EP+ and ETP+ run ProtHint internally to convert the protein FASTA into splice-site hints (prothint.gff + evidence.gff) before invoking gmes_petap.pl --EP / --ETP. ProtHint is bundled with the GeneMark-ES installer tarball under <install>/ProtHint/bin/ and with the bioconda braker3 package; there is no standalone bioconda recipe.

For the protein database, OrthoDB fungi is the standard choice:

wget https://data.orthodb.org/v11/odb11v0_proteins_fungi.fa.gz
gunzip odb11v0_proteins_fungi.fa.gz
myconote-cli predict genome_masked.fa \
    --kingdom fungi \
    --genemark-mode ep \
    --protein-fasta odb11v0_proteins_fungi.fa \
    --threads 16

docs.title: Backward compatibility
docs.text:
The pre-0.6.0 flags still work and are translated automatically:

  • --genemark (alone) → --genemark-mode es
  • --genemark + --genemark-hints <gff> → --genemark-mode et
  • --genemark-hints <gff> (alone) → --genemark-mode et

--genemark-mode always wins when passed alongside the legacy flags.

docs.title: License note
docs.text: GeneMark itself requires a free academic license from Georgia Tech (http://topaz.gatech.edu/GeneMark/). myconote-cli install predict will flag both gmes_petap.pl and prothint.py under "manual download" until the licensed tarball is on PATH.

docs.title: Using BRAKER for maximum accuracy
docs.text:
When you have both RNA-seq alignments and a fungal protein database, --use-braker is the recommended path. BRAKER is a complete predictor that internally cross-trains Augustus and GeneMark with hints from both evidence types; BRAKER3 is widely held to be the current gold standard for fungal gene prediction quality.

myconote-cli predict genome_masked.fa \
    --kingdom fungi \
    --use-braker \
    --braker-rna-bam rnaseq_sample1.bam --braker-rna-bam rnaseq_sample2.bam \
    --braker-proteins odb11v0_proteins_fungi.fa \
    --threads 16

--use-braker short-circuits the standard ab-initio + agreement-weighted consensus stack; MycoNote-CLI does not run Augustus / SNAP / GlimmerHMM / GeneMark / miniprot when BRAKER is the engine, since BRAKER produces a complete braker.gff3 that flows unchanged into the downstream update, annotate, and submit stages.

docs.title: Mode auto-detection
docs.text:
By default the BRAKER mode is selected from the inputs:

Inputs Detected mode --braker-rna-bam only BRAKER1 (--esmode plus RNA hints) --braker-proteins only BRAKER2 (--epmode) both --braker-rna-bam + --braker-proteins BRAKER3 (--etpmode) neither error — at least one evidence input is required

Pass --braker-mode <1|2|3> to override the auto-detection (e.g. force a BRAKER1 run even if you happen to have a protein FASTA on disk but want to exclude it).

docs.title: Genetic code
docs.text: --genetic-code <n> is forwarded to BRAKER as --translation_table=<n> unchanged. Set this to 12 for Candida-clade (CTG) fungi or 6 for ciliate-style codes; default is 1 (standard).

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
--use-braker requires:

  • braker.pl (bioconda braker3 provides this; the package name is braker3 even though the binary is braker.pl)
  • Augustus + Augustus-config writeable (AUGUSTUS_CONFIG_PATH); use myconote-cli setup --db augustus-fungi to populate ~/.myconote/augustus_config/ and export the variable
  • A licensed GeneMark install (EP+/ETP+ for BRAKER2/3)
  • ProtHint (bundled with the BRAKER3 conda package)

Run myconote-cli check predict to see which of these are missing.

docs.title: myconote-cli sort
docs.text:
Reorders contigs longest-first and filters out sequences below a minimum length. By default it is lossless: original contig seqids are preserved end-to-end. Renaming to NCBI-style short IDs is opt-in via --ncbi-clean.

# Default (lossless): reorder + drop anything under 500 bp, keep original names
myconote-cli sort assembly.fa --min-length 500

# NCBI-ready: also rename to scaffold_N and save the lift-over table
myconote-cli sort assembly.fa --min-length 500 --ncbi-clean --rename-table rename.tsv

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Default Description <genome.fa> required Input genome FASTA (positional) --output, -o <input>_sorted.fa Output FASTA file --min-length <bp> 0 Discard contigs shorter than this --ncbi-clean (alias --rename-contigs) off Rename contigs to <prefix>_N for NCBI's short-name requirement --prefix <str> scaffold ID prefix when --ncbi-clean is set --rename-table <file> — Write the old→new ID table (TSV); use with --ncbi-clean --keep-desc off (strip) Keep the original description after the ID --sort-by-name off (by length) Sort alphabetically instead of by length

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: File Description <input>_sorted.fa Reordered, length-filtered genome FASTA (original seqids unless --ncbi-clean) <rename-table>.tsv old→new ID mapping — only when --ncbi-clean + --rename-table are used

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Tip

Run sort first to drop junk-length contigs and get a deterministic order. The lossless default means your downstream GFF3 keeps the accessions you know; only add --ncbi-clean when preparing an NCBI submission.

With --ncbi-clean, contigs are renamed to scaffold_1, scaffold_2, … (not zero-padded). Use --prefix to customise (e.g. --prefix chr for chromosome-scale assemblies), and --rename-table to keep the lift-over map so submit (and your own records) can trace back to the originals.

docs.title: submit -- NCBI GenBank Submission
docs.text: Validates your annotation and prepares files for NCBI GenBank submission.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: myconote-cli submit <annotated.gff3> --fasta <genome.fa> --organism "Genus species" [options]

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Validates your GFF3 for NCBI compliance (duplicate IDs, orphan features, coordinates)
  2. Generates an NCBI feature table (.tbl format)
  3. Runs table2asn to produce a Sequin file (.sqn) if available
  4. Creates submission metadata files

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Flag Description --fasta <file> Genome FASTA (required) --output <dir> Output directory (default: submit_out) --organism <name> Organism name (required) --strain <name> Strain name --bioproject <acc> BioProject accession (e.g. PRJNA123456) --biosample <acc> BioSample accession (e.g. SAMN12345678) --locus-prefix <str> Locus tag prefix (default: MYCO) --genetic-code <n> Translation table (default: 1) --email <address> Contact email (written into template.sbt) --contact-first <name> Submitter first name (template.sbt) --contact-last <name> Submitter last name (template.sbt) --institution <name> Submitter institution (template.sbt) --fix-structure Repair safe structural problems before table2asn (synthesise missing gene/mRNA parents for orphan CDS); child coordinates are never altered --validate-only Only validate (including the structure check), do not generate files

Complete the .sbt or table2asn won't load it

table2asn requires a complete submission template. Provide --contact-first, --contact-last, --institution and --email, or it rejects the stub with Error loading template file. MycoNote warns when any of these is missing.

docs.title: Validation checks
docs.text: Check Type Duplicate feature IDs Error Orphan Parent references Error Coordinate ordering (start > end) Error GFF3 seqids missing from FASTA Error Missing locus_tag attributes Warning Missing product descriptions Warning

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Validate only (no files generated)
myconote-cli submit genes.gff3 --fasta genome.fa --organism "Aspergillus niger" --validate-only

# Full submission prep
myconote-cli submit annotated.gff3 --fasta genome.fa \
  --organism "Candida albicans" \
  --strain SC5314 \
  --genetic-code 12 \
  --bioproject PRJNA123456 \
  --locus-prefix CALB \
  --email narhmadey@wisc.edu

# Output files
ls submit_out/
#  annotation.tbl      -- NCBI feature table
#  annotation.fsa      -- Genome FASTA copy
#  annotation.sqn      -- Sequin file (if table2asn installed)
#  template.sbt        -- Submission template
#  structure_fixed.gff3 -- repaired GFF3 (only when --fix-structure applied repairs)

docs.title: Before submitting to NCBI
docs.text:
1. Register a BioProject for your genome
  2. Register a BioSample for your organism/strain
  3. Request a locus_tag prefix from NCBI
  4. Run myconote-cli submit --validate-only to check for errors
  5. Fix any errors, then run without --validate-only to generate files
  6. Upload the .sqn file to NCBI Submission Portal

docs.title: myconote update
docs.text:
myconote-cli update --help

update refines an initial gene annotation produced by predict using RNA-seq evidence. The default path runs PASA (with a lightweight minimap2-coverage fallback when PASA is unavailable) to add UTRs, correct intron/exon boundaries, and add alternative isoforms. See the Pipeline Overview for how update fits into the full workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
At least one of the following RNA-seq inputs is required:

  • --rna-r1 (and --rna-r2 for paired-end) — raw FASTQ reads. Trinity is invoked internally to assemble transcripts.
  • --transcripts <file> — pre-assembled transcript FASTA (Trinity output, IsoSeq, or any cDNA FASTA). Skips the Trinity step.
  • --rna-bam <file> — pre-aligned BAM. Used by the lightweight UTR fallback only; PASA re-aligns internally.

docs.title: Using Kallisto for transcript filtering
docs.text:
update --kallisto adds an abundance pre-filter step that mirrors funannotate's update flow: every transcript is assigned a TPM by kallisto quant, transcripts below --kallisto-min-tpm (default 1.0 TPM) are dropped, and only the surviving IDs are written to a pasa_kallisto_filter.txt sidecar passed to PASA's update step. This removes spurious Trinity assemblies and assembly artifacts that would otherwise feed PASA noise and inflate isoform counts.

myconote-cli update predict_out/consensus.gff3 \
    --fasta genome.fa \
    --rna-r1 reads_R1.fastq.gz \
    --rna-r2 reads_R2.fastq.gz \
    --kallisto \
    --kallisto-min-tpm 1.0 \
    --threads 16

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Use --kallisto when you have extensive RNA-seq coverage and expect a substantial fraction of Trinity assemblies to be assembly artifacts. The 1.0-TPM cut is funannotate's tested-default and works well at typical Illumina depths (≥30M paired reads).
  • Skip --kallisto when RNA-seq coverage is low (single-replicate or fewer than ~10M reads) — the 1.0-TPM threshold will over-filter and drop legitimate low-expressed transcripts. Either run without --kallisto or drop the cut substantially with --kallisto-min-tpm 0.1.
  • Skip --kallisto when your only RNA-seq input is a pre-aligned BAM (--rna-bam). Kallisto requires raw reads to pseudoalign; a BAM is rejected with a clear error.

docs.title: Outputs added under --kallisto
docs.text: Path Contents update_out/kallisto/transcripts.idx Kallisto index over the transcript FASTA update_out/kallisto/sample_NN/abundance.tsv Per-sample kallisto quant output update_out/kallisto/passing_transcripts.txt Transcript IDs that cleared the TPM filter update_out/pasa_kallisto_filter.txt The same passing-ID list at the top level

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
--kallisto requires kallisto on PATH. Install with:

myconote-cli install update          # installs kallisto + the rest of update's deps
# or directly:
conda install -c bioconda kallisto

If --kallisto is set and kallisto is missing, the run aborts with a clear error and a pointer at myconote-cli install update. There is no silent fallback.

docs.title: Citation

docs.title: Kingdom Defaults
docs.text: MycoNote-CLI ships with sensible per-kingdom defaults so you don't need to specify every parameter manually. Pass --kingdom to a pipeline command to activate these defaults. Fungi is the primary, validated target; the other kingdoms are an experimental scaffold (see the Supported Kingdoms note).

docs.title: Augustus species models
docs.text:
Kingdom Default species Notes Fungi saccharomyces_cerevisiae_S288C Ascomycota; see --clade below for a clade-aware default Plant arabidopsis Arabidopsis thaliana Animal human Homo sapiens Insect fly Drosophila melanogaster Protist toxoplasma Toxoplasma gondii

Override with --species <model> to use any installed Augustus species.

Clade-aware fungal default (--clade)

For fungi, saccharomyces_cerevisiae_S288C is a Saccharomycotina model and a poor default off that clade. Instead of hard-coding it, pass predict --clade saccharomycotina|pezizomycotina|basidiomycota to pick a clade-appropriate model (Pezizomycotina → aspergillus_nidulans, Basidiomycota → cryptococcus_neoformans_neoformans_JEC21). A fungal run with neither --species nor --clade still uses S288C but prints a warning.

docs.title: From raw contigs to NCBI-ready submission, in one binary
With built-in functional placement and AI-assisted interpretation
docs.text:
Benjamin Narh-Madey Hittinger Lab · Laboratory of Genetics University of Wisconsin–Madison narhmadey@wisc.edu

github.com/K-nie/myconote-cli · MIT · v0.2.0

docs.title: The bottleneck has moved
docs.text:
Long-read sequencing is cheap. Annotation is not.

  • funannotate — 3 fungi / day on a workstation; manual cleanup required
  • MAKER — flexible but configuration-heavy
  • BRAKER — RNA-seq gold standard, but a single pipeline step

Result: annotation, not sequencing, dictates paper timelines.

MycoNote-CLI is a single Rust binary that takes a eukaryotic genome assembly from raw contigs to NCBI-ready submission — with reproducibility baked in.

docs.title: One binary, seven commands
docs.text:
sort → mask → train → predict → update → annotate → submit

Each step is a separate subcommand. Stop anywhere. Resume anywhere. Standard formats (GFF3, FASTA, GenBank) throughout.

  • Rust — blazing-fast parallelism, no Python dependency hell
  • Per-contig parallelism — Augustus, repeat-masking, EVM all rayon-backed
  • JSON reproducibility reports — tool versions, parameters, checksums
  • Docker + Singularity — pinned dependency graphs for HPC and cloud

docs.title: Multi-predictor consensus, not single-predictor hope
docs.text:
┌─ Augustus   ─┐
         ├─ SNAP       ─┤
FASTA →  ├─ GlimmerHMM ─┼→ EVM consensus → GFF3 → annotate
         ├─ GeneMark   ─┤
         └─ miniprot   ─┘
              protein evidence
  • Weighted evidence integration — one bad predictor does not sink the call
  • Ploidy-aware allelic duplicate detection
  • 25 NCBI genetic code tables supported

docs.title: Why genetic-code correctness matters
docs.text:
Table Name When it applies 1 Standard Most eukaryotes (default) 12 Alternative Yeast Nuclear Candida CTG clade (CTG = Ser) 3 Yeast Mitochondrial Yeast mt genomes

The CTG clade reassigned CTG → Serine ~170–270 Mya.

Annotate C. albicans with table 1 and every Ser encoded by CTG reads as Leu in silico → wrong Pfam hits, wrong domain architecture, NCBI validation errors.

Santos & Tuite (1995) NAR · Krassowski et al. (2018) Nat Commun · Opulente et al. (2024) Science

docs.title: place — Y1000+ functional placement
docs.text:
Input: your annotate_out/annotations.tsv (KEGG-KO per gene) Reference: Y1000+ — 1,154 sequenced yeasts (Opulente et al. 2024) Method: KEGG-KO Jaccard similarity → ranked neighbours

Auto-predictions when reference subsets are installed:

  • Codon table — from top hit → prevents the CTG trap
  • C/N metabolic lifestyle — weighted vote across neighbours
  • Growth at 37 °C — thermotolerance / pathogenic potential
  • Ecological niche — insect gut, flower nectar, rotting wood, …

Opulente DA et al. (2024). Science 384(6694): eadj4503

docs.title: explain — AI interpretation with scientific guardrails
docs.text:
myconote-cli explain predict
  • Local Ollama backend — your data never leaves the machine
  • RAM-aware model selection — 8 GB baseline → 48 GB top tier
  • Deterministic fallback — --no-llm mode needs no model

Guardrails — where most LLM-bio tools fail:

  • Every claim must cite [knowledge:…], [paper:<doi>], [data:<file>:<line>], or [rule:…]
  • Post-hoc citation validator strips tags the model invented
  • Ethics gate — pattern-based refusal for out-of-scope queries
  • --trace shows prompt, retrieval scores, validator decisions
  • --dry-run assembles the prompt without calling the LLM

docs.title: batch — many genomes, one command
docs.text:
# From a sample sheet
myconote-cli batch samples.tsv --parallel 4

# HTCondor submit-file generation for HPC
myconote-cli batch genomes/ --condor --condor-mem 64G
  • Directory mode or sample sheet (TSV with per-genome settings)
  • Resume after partial failure — no recomputation
  • HTCondor first-class support — generates condor.sub + per-genome wrappers
  • Live dashboard for local parallel runs

docs.title: compare — real N-genome orthology
docs.text:
OrthoFinder wrapping — not a toy.

  • DendroBLAST default (fast) or MSA mode (MAFFT + trimAl)
  • Supermatrix bridge into phylogeny — concatenated single-copy orthologs → IQ-TREE species tree
  • Tiered genome-count caps — 5 fungi / 3 Arabidopsis-class dicots / 2 maize-class monocots (because OrthoFinder scales as n²)
  • Disambiguates duplicate genome names before feeding to OrthoFinder
myconote-cli compare --kingdom fungi proteomes/

docs.text:
Brettanomyces bruxellensis (novel assembly, 30 contigs, 12.9 Mb)

Step Time Result predict (Augustus) ~3 min 5,218 genes annotate (MMseqs2) ~1.5 min 75% with product names annotate (Pfam, hmmsearch) ~7 min 85.6% with domains NCBI validation <1 s PASSED (0 errors)

docs.text:

  • JSON run reports — every parameter, tool version, checksum
  • Semantic versioning — v0.2.0 changelog explicit about prototypes that did not ship
  • MIT licence — reuse freely with attribution
  • CI — GitHub Actions (fmt + clippy + test + cargo-audit)

docs.title: What MycoNote-CLI does NOT do
docs.text:
Honest limitations matter for a methods paper.

  • Functional assignments are hypotheses, not facts — a 30 % identity MMseqs2 hit is a best guess
  • Gene prediction still makes mistakes, especially at UTRs and in repeat-rich regions
  • LLM outputs are suggestive, not definitive — verify against your organism and aims
  • v0.2.0 has weeks of community testing, not years — validate critical calls against a second tool
  • Comprehensive 8-genome benchmark vs funannotate / MAKER / BRAKER is planned, not yet run

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
• Comprehensive benchmark — 8 reference genomes × 4 tools × 3 replicates on the GLBRC HTCondor pool
  • Interactive web UI — upload FASTA, watch pipeline progress, download GenBank
  • More Augustus training species — expanding beyond the default fungal set
  • Integration with existing community pipelines where it adds value, not replaces

docs.title: Take-home
docs.text:
1. One binary, seven commands — annotation without the dependency labyrinth
  2. Y1000+ placement catches silent errors (codon table, lifestyle mismatch) before they ruin a paper
  3. AI interpretation with real guardrails — citation validation, ethics gate, deterministic rules fallback — not another hallucination engine
  4. MIT, reproducible, open — clone, cite, contribute
